hyperiongrp.wd3.myworkdayjobs.com/broadb.description_excerpt:
Who are we?
Howden is a global insurance group with employee ownership at its heart. Together, we have pushed the boundaries of insurance. We are united by a shared passion and no-limits mindset, and our strength lies in our ability to collaborate as a powerful international team comprised of 24,000 employees spanning over 56 countries.
People join Howden for many different reasons, but they stay for the same one: our culture. It’s what sets us apart, and the reason our employees have been turning down headhunters for years. Whatever your priorities – work / life balance, career progression, sustainability, volunteering – you’ll find like-minded people driving change at Howden.
The role
Howden is moving from deploying AI tools to embedding AI into how the business actually works. The Group AI Function has a clear mandate to drive that shift, and the next phase demands stronger technical governance, sharper architecture thinking, and closer oversight of what’s being built across the organisation.
The AI Technical Lead is the technical authority inside the function. The role owns architecture governance, leads the assessment of AI tools and vendors, and provides technical oversight across AI initiatives running inside Howden and with external delivery partners. When engineering work is happening — whether done internally or by third parties — this role ensures it’s done to the right standard and that Howden retains genuine ownership of the output.
This is an individual contributor role. It sits at the centre of a programme that touches every part of the Group, with direct access to senior stakeholders and real influence over how our AI capability develops.
Key responsibilities
Architecture governance
Own the technical governance process for AI tools and platforms across the Group. Lead Architecture Review Board submissions, produce architecture and security design documentation, and work alongside Enterprise Architecture as the AI function’s technical representative. The goal is coherent, well-governed AI infrastructure — not a patchwork of unconnected tools.
Vendor and tooling assessment
Lead the technical evaluation of inbound AI vendors and tools. Build a repeatable assessment framework that gives the Head of AI a clear, evidence-based view of what to adopt, what to decline, and where to build instead. Ensure that tooling decisions are grounded in architecture fit, security, data governance, and commercial sense — not just functionality.
Oversight of AI delivery
AI initiatives are running across multiple divisions, and external partners are actively involved in delivery. This role provides the technical oversight that ensures quality, protects Howden’s IP, and prevents the organisation from becoming dependent on third parties for capability it should own internally. This isn’t a hands-off review role — it requires enough depth to challenge, guide, and take accountability for outcomes.
Technical enablement
Set and maintain technical standards for how AI is built across the business — covering areas like agent development, knowledge retrieval, prompt engineering, and evaluation. Support colleagues and divisional AI leads who are building or deploying AI, and translate technical constraints into practical guidance that people can actually use.
Technical partnership to the Head of AI
Provide the technical grounding that allows the Head of AI to make well-informed decisions quickly. This means flagging risks, pressure-testing proposals, and being a genuine thought partner — not just an executor. The function is small and the relationship needs to work closely.
Background and experience
Essential
Desirable
Hands-on experience with large language models, retrieval systems, and agent frameworks
Exposure to insurance or another regulated industry
Cloud-native AI architecture experience
Experience with enterprise AI platform governance
Track record writing architecture or security design documentation
Familiarity with AI evaluation and quality assurance approaches
Ability to assess AI vendors and tooling rigorously and independently
Experience overseeing third-party AI delivery
Strong communication — equally comfortable with engineers and senior leaders
Previous work in an architecture review or governance context
Intellectually curious, low-ego, and comfortable moving fast in ambiguous conditions
Experience in a small, high-output team
What good looks like
Over the first year, success in this role means:
• Architecture governance runs smoothly — new tools are assessed, documented, and reviewed without creating bottlenecks or risk
• A repeatable vendor assessment process is in place and being used consistently
• Technical oversight of external delivery partners is formalised and effective
• AI standards and best practices are being adopted across the business, not just documented
• Howden is demonstrably building internal AI capability rather than outsourcing it
• The Head of AI has a technical partner who makes decision-making faster and better
Working in the Group AI Function
The Group AI Function is deliberately small. We work directly with senior stakeholders, operate across the whole Group, and move between strategy and execution without much ceremony. The Head of AI reports to the Group CTO and works closely with divisional leadership. The pace is real and the problems are interesting.
The culture values getting things right over looking right. Direct, honest, curious — and not precious about hierarchy or process for its own sake. The role carries real scope from day one and genuine influence over how the function and the broader AI capability develops.
What do we offer in return?
A career that you define. At Howden, we value diversity – there is no one Howden type. Instead, we’re looking for individuals who share the same values as us:
•
Our successes have all come from someone brave enough to try something new
•
We support each other in the small everyday moments and the bigger challenges
•
We are determined to make a positive difference at work and beyond
Reasonable adjustments
We're committed to providing reasonable accommodations at Howden to ensure that our positions align well with your needs.  Besides the usual adjustments such as software, IT, and office setups, we can also accommodate other changes such as flexible hours* or hybrid working*.
If you're excited by this role but have some doubts about whether it’s the right fit for you, send us your application – if your profile fits the role’s criteria, we will be in touch to assist in helping to get you set up with any reasonable adjustments you may require.
*Not all positions can accommodate changes to working hours or locations. Reach out to your Recruitment Partner if you want to know more.

Job Description
Growth Marketing & Acquisition Manager
Location: Farnborough

About Pregnancy+
Pregnancy+ is the world’s most downloaded pregnancy app, trusted by millions of mums and mums-to-be worldwide. Our mission is to improve the health literacy, happiness, and well-being of every parent-to-be. We blend trusted information with uplifting, intuitive, and inclusive experiences to be the most nurturing companion throughout the pregnancy journey and beyond into postpartum. We support over 6 million active users each month and continue to grow as a leading platform within Philips’ Worry-Free Parenting team, combining empathy, innovation, and design excellence to make every moment feel effortless and supported.
Your Role
We’re looking for a Growth Marketing & Acquisition Manager to own how Pregnancy+ grows its user base worldwide. You’ll take full ownership of our acquisition strategy across every channel, paid and unpaid, and the measurement that proves what is actually working. You’ll move us away from a narrow, single-channel approach and build a genuine acquisition portfolio: paid social and search, app store optimisation, organic and emerging channels, and the creative engine that powers all of them.
Your starting point is always strategic: working out how we grow, where the next wave of acquisition growth will come from, which new channels to open, where the efficiency gains are hiding, and how the mix should evolve over time. From there, you decide how to execute against that plan, calling on a network of freelancers, agencies, and specialist partners, alongside internal support from product, design, content, and analytics, to deliver at scale. You’ll be the single point of accountability for our cost of acquisition and the growth of our active user base.
That said, this is not a hands-off role. You should be an operator who is comfortable getting your hands dirty: turning a campaign around fast, shipping a landing page test, fixing a tracking issue, or getting something live yourself when speed matters more than process. The best person for this pairs the strategic view with the instinct and ability to execute.
What You’ll Do:
Own the full acquisition portfolio
• Set and own the acquisition strategy across all channels: paid social (Meta, TikTok), paid search (Google UAC / App Campaigns), Apple Search Ads, app store optimisation (ASO), SEO, and emerging channels such as generative engine optimisation (GEO) and creator-led growth for AI-driven discovery, rather than optimising any single one in isolation.
• Own cost of acquisition and active user growth as your headline metrics, and make evidence-based decisions about where the next pound of spend or hour of effort should go.
• Continuously rebalance the channel mix and test new or under-exploited channels as clear bets, doubling down on what works and retiring what doesn’t.
Drive creative velocity and testing
• Treat creative as the primary lever for improving acquisition efficiency, not an afterthought to budget management.
• Build a high-output creative engine through UGC specialists, creators, freelancers, and agency partners, increasing the volume and variety of concepts we test by an order of magnitude.
• Write sharp creative briefs grounded in audience insight, run structured testing frameworks, and feed winning signals back into the platforms and the wider funnel.
Direct agencies, freelancers, and specialists
• Source, onboard, brief, and manage a lean network of specialist partners (mobile UA agencies, creative producers, channel specialists), bringing in new specialists as the strategy demands rather than building a large in-house team.
• Hold partners accountable to clear outcomes and benchmarks, while staying close enough to the detail to challenge their work and step in when needed.
Build measurement and incrementality infrastructure
• Move us beyond optimising on installs toward measuring real downstream value and incremental impact.
• Own the measurement stack (attribution, event tracking, value-based signals) and run regular incrementality testing so we can trust what is genuinely driving growth.
• Automate the reporting and account checks that currently eat time, and simplify campaign structures so more effort goes into creative and strategy and less into manually moving budgets between campaigns and markets.
Orchestrate cross-functional growth
• Partner with content, commercial, and partnership teams to unlock acquisition through healthcare, retail, and creator relationships that paid media alone cannot reach.
• Work with the lifecycle and CRM function to ensure acquisition connects cleanly into onboarding, activation, and retention, not just top-of-funnel installs.
• Collaborate with product and engineering to improve store conversion, onboarding, and the in-product moments that compound acquisition into long-term value.
What We’re Looking For
• At least 5 years in user acquisition for consumer mobile apps, with meaningful time spent owning strategy across multiple channels and markets, not solely executing in one.
• A track record of improving cost of acquisition through creative testing, not just spend management, grounded in a current understanding of how modern paid platforms work.
• Strong command of mobile measurement (attribution, MMPs, event and value tracking, and incrementality testing), with the analytical instinct to interpret data, stay sceptical of vanity metrics like raw installs, and turn findings into clear, prioritised action and honest trade-offs.
• Experience selecting, onboarding, and directing agencies, freelancers, and specialists to deliver outcomes rather than just activity.
• A scrappy, bias-to-action operator who would rather ship and learn than perfect and wait, and who can roll up their sleeves and execute themselves when speed demands it.
• Genuine curiosity about emerging channels (GEO, creator and partnership-led growth) alongside strong working knowledge of established ones (SEO, ASO) and a habit of testing new opportunities early.
• Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with the credibility to influence product, engineering, analytics, and commercial stakeholders.
• The ability to translate brand strategy into channel execution — you understand that creative, tone, and messaging consistency across Meta, TikTok, and search directly impact performance outcomes. You’re as comfortable discussing CAC, ROAS, and downstream event optimisation as you are briefing a creator on what makes Pregnancy+ feel distinctly warm, trusted, and inclusive.

Global’s Data team is looking for a Senior Machine Learning Engineer to build, deploy and scale machine learning solutions—turning data science ideas into robust, production-grade products.

Model Development & Optimisation: Design, build and optimise ML and deep-learning models—including for ad targeting and attribution—with a focus on scalability, performance and accuracy, and prototype and evaluate new approaches.

ML Pipelines & Real-Time Inference: Build and maintain robust end-to-end ML pipelines covering training, validation, deployment and monitoring, and develop real-time inference systems with low latency and high throughput.
•
Monitoring & Reliability: Implement model monitoring, drift detection, alerting and retraining, and optimise models for reliability and cost efficiency in AWS.

Collaboration & Enablement: Partner with data engineers to integrate ML workflows into wider platforms (Spark, Databricks), and share best practice and mentor other technical professionals.

Think Big: Build ML and AI solutions that shape products, improve decision-making and unlock growth.
•
Own It: Take ideas from concept to production and see the impact of your work in the real world.

Keep it Simple: Turn complex technical challenges into scalable, practical solutions.
•
Better Together: Work with smart, supportive people across data, engineering, analytics and the wider business.

In your first few months, you’ll have:
•
Built ML products that deliver measurable value, improving Global’s capabilities in areas such as ad targeting and attribution.
•
Ensured ML models are reliably deployed, monitored and maintained, with automated, reproducible and scalable pipelines.
•
Built real-time systems that operate efficiently and reliably under production demand.
•
Developed a strong understanding of Global’s data ecosystem, tools and operating model, particularly within DAX.

•
Production ML experience: You’ve delivered ML and deep-learning projects at high data volume commercially, owning deployment, CI/CD, monitoring and lifecycle management.
•
Strong Python: Solid Python with PyTorch or similar ML frameworks.
•
Model evaluation: You diagnose why models underperform across data, features and architecture, and make reasoned trade-offs.
•
Real-time & distributed ML: A strong grasp of production inference patterns, plus Spark and distributed data processing.
•
Reproducibility & tooling: Reproducible environments (UV/Docker) and MLflow or equivalent, on AWS with Spark, Databricks and Snowflake.
•
Engineering mindset: A focus on reliability, maintainability and continuous improvement.

Every day, millions of people rely on transport to access the people, places and opportunities that matter most. At Arriva, we're shaping the future of passenger transport and investing in the people who will help lead it.
We are one of Europe's leading passenger transport partners, helping people get to work, education, healthcare, family and the moments that matter. Operating across 11 countries, with around 35,000 colleagues and more than 1.5 billion passenger journeys each year, we're a business with the scale to make a difference and the ambition to keep moving forward.
Through our Graduate Programme, we're looking for talented graduates who are curious, motivated to learn and ready to grow their careers with us.
If you're ready to make an impact, we'd love to hear from you.
The Graduate Opportunity
As a Trainee Solicitor on our Graduate Programme, you'll join our in-house Legal team on a two-year training contract designed to take you through qualification as a solicitor of England and Wales. You’ll gain hands-on experience across a range of legal specialisms, supervised throughout by qualified solicitors.
Over two years, you'll complete structured placements across our legal function, developing a broad understanding of how legal advice supports one of Europe's leading passenger transport businesses.
From supporting operational teams, commercial growth projects and regulatory compliance to working on company secretarial matters and personal injury cases, you'll play a genuine role in helping the business navigate complex legal challenges while building the experience needed for your future legal career.
This is a full-time, two-year training contract. We provide the supervision, training and practical experience you need to qualify as a solicitor at the end of it.
Throughout your training contract you’ll have:
• Day-to-day supervision, we will review your work, give you regular feedback and increase your responsibility as your confidence grows
• A supervisor for each seat, plus a senior solicitor who oversees your training across the full two years
• Regular progress reviews mapped to the SRA’s Statement of Solicitor Competence, so you always know where you stand and what to focus on next
• Work that counts as Qualifying Work Experience (QWE) under the Solicitors Qualifying Examination (SQE) route, confirmed with the SRA by a solicitor in our team
• A structured learning programme covering legal skills, professional conduct and ethics, and commercial awareness
Location: This role is based at our Sunderland office and operates on a hybrid basis, with a minimum of three days per week in the office.
What We’re Looking For:
We're not expecting you to have all the answers. We're looking for graduates with curiosity, drive and the confidence to keep learning. People who take ownership, build positive relationships and want to make a meaningful contribution from day one.
What matters most is your potential. We're looking for people who are eager to learn, motivated to grow and ready to develop their Arriva Graduate EDGE.
About You:
We're open to applications from graduates of all degree disciplines. To be eligible for this role you’ll need to have passed both SQE1 and SQE2 before the programme starts, and be ready to commence a training contract.
We're particularly interested in people who:
• Are curious, proactive and eager to learn
• Enjoy solving problems and thinking critically
• Have strong communication and relationship-building skills
• Can analyse information and apply sound judgement
• Enjoy working collaboratively with a range of stakeholders
• Have excellent attention to detail and professionalism
• Are interested in commercial law and the wider business environment
• Aspire to build a career as a qualified solicitor
The Graduate Programme
Alongside your role, you'll also be part of our two-year graduate development programme, benefiting from structured learning, mentoring, exposure to senior leaders and a connected graduate network across Arriva.
The breadth of experience gained throughout the programme will help you build a strong foundation for your future legal career.
Alongside practical experience across multiple legal specialisms, you'll have opportunities to develop your commercial awareness, stakeholder management and professional skills while working towards becoming qualified as a solicitor.
Eligibility Requirements
To be considered for this opportunity, you'll need:
• To be on track to achieve, or have already achieved, a degree (2:1 preferred, with strong 2:2 applications considered)
• To have passed both SQE1 and SQE2 before September 2027 and be eligible to commence a training contract
• The right to work in the UK permanently
• Availability to join the programme in September 2027
• Willingness to travel where required as part of the programme

Role Description:
We are seeking a motivated and analytically driven Security Detection & Response Analyst (SDR) to join the GIS Monitoring and Triage team. This role supports cybersecurity operations across threat detection, investigation, response, and continuous service improvement.
The ideal candidate will have security practitioner experience with strong analytical aptitude and foundational technical skills, who contributes to the detection and response lifecycle by supporting investigations and response activities under guidance.
This role focuses on developing the ability to analyse security events, build contextual understanding of threats, and progressively operate with increasing independence across multiple security domains. The analyst will work alongside experienced practitioners to validate detections, investigate events, and execute response actions while building foundational skills in automation, orchestration, and AI-driven technologies.
Working Pattern:
This is a full-time role (40 hours per week), with standard working hours of 7:00AM to 6:00PM 4 days per week (Sunday to Wednesday or Wednesday to Saturday) to align with the nature of the support provided by the team. Flexibility may occasionally be required to support business, operational, or project deliverables.
Responsibilities:
• Support the detection and response lifecycle (detect → investigate → respond → improve) by triaging alerts and analysing logs and telemetry from multiple sources to assess potential security events
• Correlate and analyse data across endpoint, identity, network, and application sources to develop context and determine whether activity is benign or suspicious
• Assist in the investigation of security events by applying structured, hypothesis-driven analysis and escalating complex or high-risk findings to more senior analysts
• Perform guided response activities under supervision, including alert enrichment, containment support, documentation, and coordination with more senior team members during active investigations
• Validate alerts and contribute to improving detection fidelity by identifying false positives and providing feedback to enhance detection logic and coverage
• Contribute to the development and refinement of investigation guides, runbooks, and playbooks, while learning to leverage automation, SOAR workflows, and AI-assisted tools to improve efficiency
• Identify gaps in telemetry, monitoring, or processes and escalate improvement opportunities to support continuous enhancement of detection and response capabilities
What we’re looking for:
• A number of years hands on experience in cybersecurity, security operations, IT support, or related technical fields (internships, academic projects, or equivalent experience included)
• Foundational knowledge of security detection, investigation, or incident response principles, with a demonstrated ability to learn and apply concepts across multiple domains
• Basic experience with log analysis and telemetry interpretation, including familiarity with querying or analyzing data using tools such as SIEM platforms or query languages (KQL, SPL, SQL, or similar)
• Exposure to security platforms and technologies such as SIEM, EDR/XDR, identity systems, or cloud environments
• Foundational understanding of common attacker tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs), with familiarity of frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK
• Analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to follow structured investigation processes and document findings clearly
• Effective communication skills, including the ability to provide clear updates and collaborate with team members during investigations
• Willingness to learn, take direction, and progressively develop independent decision-making capabilities in security operations environments
Skills that will help:
• Deep analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to follow structured investigation processes and document findings clearly
• Effective communication skills, including the ability to provide clear updates and collaborate with team members during investigations

Delivering predominantly electronic and electro-mechanical product lines, this site specialises in fuel measurement systems, emergency oxygen systems, barometrics, and complex electro-mechanical assemblies.
Ontic, a leading licensor and manufacturer of complex engineering parts for the global aerospace and defence industries, is now recruiting for a Health & Safety Manager to join our Bishops Cleeve site in Cheltenham.
You’ll play a key role in shaping and embedding a positive health and safety culture across the site, ensuring that our operations continue to meet the highest standards of safety, compliance, and employee well-being.
This role will be based at our Ontic Bishops Cleeve site, although occasional travel between our Gloucestershire sites should be expected.

Reporting directly to the Site Director, you'll be responsible for leading our approach to environmental, health and safety risks across our Bishops Cleeve site. This is an opportunity to make a meaningful impact, influencing how EHS is understood, valued and embedded across a complex and evolving manufacturing environment. You will lead the development and implementation of our EHS management systems, strengthen our safety culture and work collaboratively with leaders and employees to ensure EHS is an integral part of operational excellence.
We are looking for someone who can balance strong technical knowledge with a pragmatic, engaging and people-focused approach and someone who sees EHS not simply as a compliance function, but as an enabler of safe, efficient and sustainable operations.
The role is based at our Bishops Cleeve facility, with occasional travel between our Gloucestershire sites.

• Champion a positive, proactive and inclusive EHS culture where everyone understands their responsibilities and feels empowered to contribute to a safer workplace.
• Act as a trusted advisor to the Site Director and wider leadership team, providing strategic direction and constructive challenge on EHS matters.
• Promote employee engagement, consultation and participation in identifying risks, developing solutions and driving improvements.
• Facilitate effective EHS committees, leadership reviews and employee consultation.
• Lead the ongoing development, implementation and continuous improvement of the site's EHS management systems, aligned with ISO 45001 principles and relevant legislative requirements.
• Collaborate with Facilities on all aspects of facility development, maintenance, contractor management and improvement.
• Support the safe introduction, modification and recommissioning of equipment, processes and facilities.
• Develop, maintain and improve EHS policies, procedures, risk assessments and safe systems of work.
• Attend site-specific leadership meetings and site walks.
• Deliver proactive site-wide EHS training.
• Lead EHS assurance activities, including audits, inspections, performance reviews and corrective action management.
• Provide technical guidance on occupational health, hazardous substances, machinery safety, electrical safety, contractor management and other manufacturing-related risks.
• Lead investigations, root cause analysis and organisational learning.
• Develop and monitor meaningful EHS performance indicators that measure both compliance and proactive risk management.
• Provide clear, insightful EHS reporting to site leadership, identifying trends, priorities and opportunities for improvement.
• Drive the timely and sustainable closure of EHS actions, ensuring improvements are embedded into everyday operations.
• Collaborate with the wider Ontic EHS community to share best practice and support organisational improvement.
About You
At Ontic, our culture is integral to making sure we enjoy our work and deliver for our customers. While we look for the right skillset, we're also looking for someone who will thrive within our culture of recognition and empowerment.

We are looking for a confident, credible and engaging EHS professional who combines technical expertise with strong leadership and influencing skills.
You will be passionate about developing people, improving systems and creating an environment where safety is genuinely owned by everyone, not just the EHS function.
You'll be comfortable operating at both strategic and operational levels, from influencing senior leaders and developing long-term improvement plans to working directly with employees to understand practical challenges and deliver effective solutions.
Technical knowledge in the following areas: COSHH, DSEAR, radiation safety, electrical and high-voltage safety, Occupational Hygiene, pressure systems, machinery safety and ergonomics.

• NEBOSH Level 6 National Diploma in Occupational Health and Safety (or recognised equivalent).

Industry Technology Strategy & Architecture leads at the intersection of business and technology, driving maximum client value through the exploitation of AI, technology and data. We serve as the primary architect of our clients' industry-relevant technology estate, defining future-state visions, building the business case for change, and designing the enterprise architecture that turns ambition into an executable roadmap.

• Own workstreams and delivery within technology strategy engagements, shaping scope, mobilising teams, managing plans, risks, issues, client expectations and project commercials, and delivering to agreed time, budget and quality.

• Help shape enterprise AI and data strategies, including roadmaps for scaling enterprise AI and foundation data.

• Deep capability in technology strategy, business model strategy, technology assessment, competitor analysis, market intelligence, partner ecosystem strategy and application strategy.

We're very interested in hearing from you if you have some or all of the following.

• Strong understanding of industry operations, dynamics and trends, developed through experience in one or more sectors such as financial services, telecommunications, technology, resources and utilities, retail or consumer goods.

At Accenture in addition to a competitive salary, you will also have an extensive benefits package, private medical insurance and 3 extra days leave per year for charitable work of your choice!

Who are we?
Equinix is the world’s digital infrastructure company®, shortening the path to connectivity to enable the innovations that enrich our work, life and planet.
A place where bold ideas are welcomed, human connection is valued, and everyone has the opportunity to shape their future.
A career at Equinix means being at the center of shaping what comes next and amplifying customer value through innovation and impact. You’ll work across teams, influence key decisions, and help shape the path forward. You’ll find belonging, purpose, and a team that welcomes you—because when you feel valued, you’re empowered to do your best work.
We are looking for a Senior Director to lead our EMEA Enterprise Customer Success Management organization at an important point in the evolution of Customer Success Management at Equinix.  This leader will be responsible for translating our global Customer Success Management strategy into a value-led, data-driven regional operating model that strengthens customer relationships, improves value realization, identifies and mitigates risk, and drives predictable retention, renewals and growth.
The role requires more than operating an established Customer Success Management organization. We are looking for a builder and transformation leader who can help shape how Customer Success operates - combining high-touch customer engagement with data, digital capabilities, automation and AI to create a more proactive and scalable customer experience.  The Senior Director will lead CSM teams across EMEA and serve as a senior Customer Success partner to EMEA Sales leadership and teams across Equinix. Success will require the ability to set a clear vision, simplify complexity, develop strong leaders, and turn strategy into consistent execution across a diverse region.
Key Responsibilities:
Lead a value-led Customer Success organization
• Build a culture in which Customer Success begins with understanding customer priorities and desired outcomes. Ensure CSMs translate those priorities into Success Plans, value realization, adoption strategies, executive engagement and measurable customer outcomes.
Own retention, renewals and commercial performance
• Be accountable for regional retention and renewal performance and predictability. Establish disciplined renewal management, forecasting and risk practices while strengthening CSM commercial acumen and accountability. Partner closely with Sales on renewal strategy, expansion opportunities and long-term customer value.
Build a proactive, data-driven engagement model
• Use customer health, risk, lifecycle, commercial and behavioral signals to help CSMs prioritize where and how they engage. Drive a shift from reactive account management toward proactive engagement focused on value, risk, renewal and growth.
• Operationalize the global Customer Success Management model across EMEA
• Translate global coverage, segmentation and engagement standards into disciplined regional execution while accounting for the needs of EMEA customers and markets. Establish clear expectations engagement models and ensure consistent execution of core Customer Success Management motions.
Scale Customer Success through digital, automation and AI
• Champion the use of technology to increase CSM capacity and improve the customer experience. Partner with global teams to incorporate digital journeys, automation, AI and agentic capabilities into the Customer Success operating model allowing CSMs to focus their time where human relationships, judgment and expertise create the greatest value.
• Create consistent customer engagement and value rhythms
• Drive consistent execution of Success Planning, Customer Business Reviews, health and risk management, renewal readiness and executive engagement. Ensure these motions are focused on customer outcomes rather than activity completion.
Partner deeply with EMEA Sales and cross-functional leaders
• Serve as the senior Customer Success counterpart to EMEA Sales leadership. Build strong partnerships across Sales, Service Management, Renewals, Support, Product, Marketing, Operations, Finance and other teams to create a coordinated post-sale customer experience and remove barriers to customer outcomes.
Clarify CSM and Service Management accountability
• Help establish clear accountability between value-led Customer Success Management and operational Service Management. Reduce unnecessary handoffs, eliminate ambiguity and ensure CSM capacity remains focused on customer value, retention and growth.
Manage material customer and commercial risk
• Provide executive oversight for significant customer, relationship and renewal risks that cannot be resolved at the account or manager level. Ensure risks are identified early, clearly understood and addressed cross-functionally.
• Build and develop an exceptional regional leadership team
• Lead and coach CSM leaders across multiple EMEA markets. Build leadership capability in value articulation, commercial acumen, executive engagement, change leadership and disciplined execution. Own regional workforce planning and ensure organizational capabilities evolve alongside the Customer Success model.
Lead transformation and continuous improvement
• Create belief in the future-state Customer Success model and translate transformation strategy into clear expectations and behaviors. Challenge legacy practices, remove barriers to change, and establish a culture of measurement, experimentation and continuous improvement.
Skills, Experience & Qualifications
We are looking for a leader who brings:
• Extensive experience leading Customer Success or related GTM organizations, including leadership of leaders across multiple countries and markets.

•
Responsibilities will include managing and delivering projects, leading complex analysis, and providing oversight and support to junior staff.

ICE / IStructE / IMechE Chartered status, or planning to submit for professional review within the next year.

Eligible to obtain UK security clearance.

Able to demonstrate experience in solving complex problems and motivated to take the next step in your career by leading challenging projects.

About the opportunity:
Provide leadership in environmental and sustainability performance for Sizewell C (SZC), ensuring full compliance with environmental permits, licences, and commitments across a nationally significant nuclear construction project. Lead the site-based Environment & Sustainability team and act as the main interface with regulators, contractors, and SZC project leaders.
Sizewell C is constructing a major nuclear power station in Suffolk. The role supports compliance through construction, installation, commissioning, and handover to operations. The E&S Manager sits in the Site Construction Delivery Team, reporting to the Head of Site Compliance. The project operates under strict environmental frameworks (DCO, permits, licences) and is subject to high public and regulatory scrutiny.
The role oversees a multidisciplinary E&S team (10 people), influences Tier 1 contractors, and manages environmental monitoring budgets.
Key Responsibilities
• Provide clear leadership to E&S teams and Tier 1 contractors.
• Ensure full compliance with environmental permits, licences, consents, and ISO 14001.
• Oversee site inspections, surveillance, and performance monitoring.
• Ensure significant environmental aspects are identified, managed, and mitigated.
• Drive environmental and sustainability performance across SZC and supply chain.
• Promote world‑class environmental behaviours and best practice.
• Lead environmental investigations and implement performance improvements.
• Act as primary interface with environmental regulators (e.g., Environment Agency).
• Build strong working relationships with internal teams, contractors, and public bodies.
• Provide a professional service on all environmental and regulatory matters.
• Develop and implement KPIs and reporting to drive continuous improvement.
• Ensure department processes, resourcing, and quality standards meet SZC requirements.
• Support delivery teams across pre‑construction, construction, and commissioning phases.
• Embed lessons learned and support the One Team culture with Tier 1 contractors.
Here's What You'll Need:
• Extensive experience leading E&S teams on major, highly regulated construction projects.
• Strong understanding of environmental permits, licences, and compliance arrangements.
• Broad construction knowledge (civils → mechanical → electrical → commissioning).
• Strong leadership, influencing, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
• Ability to work across technical disciplines and operate effectively from site to boardroom.
• High standards of organisation, detail, assurance, and professional judgement.
• Understanding of sustainability opportunities and constraints on major projects.
• Degree in Environmental discipline.
• Strong leadership experience.
• Extensive client & principal contractor experience managing environmental issues on large infrastructure or engineering projects.
• Experience working with regulators and managing regulatory commitments.
• Experience implementing management systems and environmental controls.
Our Culture
Our values stand on a foundation of safety, integrity, inclusion and diversity. We put people at the heart of our business, and we genuinely believe that we all succeed by supporting one another through our culture of caring. We value positive mental health and a sense of belonging for all employees.
We aim to embed inclusion in everything we do. We know that if we are inclusive, we’re more connected, and we’re more creative. To make electronics, you need chips, wafers, transistors, reticles, and... To make these, you must see, test and manufacture them at scale—faster and better than ever before. That's where KLA comes in. Whether you're early in your career or an experienced professional, you'll solve complex challenges, work alongside brilliant minds and help shape the future of technology.
Group/Division
The Semiconductor Products and Customers (Semi PC) business unit designs, builds and sells KLA’s product portfolio to help chip manufacturers meet high-quality standards for technologies like AI, data centers, automotive and electronic devices. Our inspection, metrology, and analytics systems detect and monitor defects across logic and memory chips, specialty semiconductors, wafers, reticles, advanced packaging, process equipment and materials. We also develop technologies for specialty processes, IC substrates, and PCB manufacturing, including etch and deposition, component inspection, and imaging and analytics. The SPTS division provides advanced wafer processing solutions—including etch, deposition and vapor-based technologies—designed for R&D through high-volume production. With a global presence and strong customer support network, SPTS helps manufacturers across industries improve performance, yield and cost-efficiency. It also offers comprehensive service and spare parts through a worldwide network of service centers and qualified local agents.
What You'll Do
In this role, you will play a key part in advancing business priorities by delivering high-impact work across your area of expertise.
Primary Purpose of Role
Working in the Product Marketing Operations (PM Ops) team within SPTS, the Product Marketing Coordinator (PMC) is responsible for supporting multiple operational aspects of the Product Marketing function, enabling Product Marketing Managers to focus on strategic tasks and customer engagement.
The primary focus of the PMC is to create and manage the marketing-defined machine build specification requirements that Manufacturing Operations will work to, known within the organisation as the System Configuration Document (SCD).
Key Responsibilities & Areas of Involvement
Working alongside other Product Marketing Coordinators, the role will involve extensive interaction with Sales, Manufacturing Operations, Engineering and Marketing peers.
System Configuration Document (SCD) Coordination
• Slot plan demand tracking
• SCD coordination, generation and revision control
• Final Quote Review coordination and hosting
• Interaction with SAP sub-contractors
Sample Demonstration Coordination
• Demo Request Form (DRF) review coordination & responses to sales
• Sample Demo Schedule Host & updates to sales
• Demo Statistics support for management review
• Live Demo/Factory Visit logistics
RFQ Response Coordination
When sized appropriately, a longer-term objective for the PM Ops team will be to coordinate (and contribute to) review and response of machine specifications along with quote guidance to Sales Operations, releasing Product Marketing Managers to focus on more strategic and customer-facing activities.
Knowledge of some of the following would be advantageous:
Some knowledge of Semiconductor Processing equipment would be beneficial but is not mandatory.
The candidate is expected to be familiar with SAP, Powerpoint and Excel spreadsheets.
Personal skills
• Enthusiastic with a positive attitude
• Self-motivated and proactive
• Open, co-operative, empathetic
• Excellent attention to detail
• Able to work under pressure and to tight deadlines
• Able to work across all levels within the company, and across regions
• Excellent communication skills
What We Offer
• 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays
• Share scheme
• Contributory pension scheme
• Cash health plan
• Cycle to Work scheme
• Global bonus plan
• Employee rewards scheme
• Life assurance
Minimum Qualifications
Master's Level Degree; Bachelor's Level Degree and related work experience
About KLA
We provide advanced inspection tools, metrology systems, process solutions, and computational analytics that make electronics possible, tackling complex challenges. From electron and photon optics to machine learning and data analytics, we seek perfection at the most fundamental level of matter in the universe. If you want to make electronics that push industries forward and make the world a better place, join us.

○ Support a range of change initiatives, strategic projects and capital-related developments across the business.

○ Knowledge of Solvency UK and the wider UK regulatory framework.

○ Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage confidently with senior stakeholders.

○ The ability to balance strong technical understanding with commercial awareness and practical decision making.

Practice Group / Department:
EMEA IT Applications
Job Description
Norton Rose Fulbright is a global law firm with more than 3,000 lawyers advising clients across locations in the United States, Europe, Canada, Latin America, Asia, Australia, Africa and the Middle East. We provide a full scope of legal services to the world’s preeminent corporations and financial institutions.
Our vision is to be a world class business, profitable, ambitious, cooperative and considerate, supporting our clients and people through our global business principles of Quality, Unity and Integrity.
With over 7,000 employees worldwide, our culture is the thread that connects us. Our strategy and culture are closed connected – defined by shared ambition, global collaboration and a one-team mindset. We believe pioneering work happens when people are empowered to think beyond boundaries, explore new opportunities and grow through diverse experiences. Alongside the right skills and experience, we are looking for people who are innovative, commercially minded, and motivated by the impact of the work they do – ready to share in our ambition and help shape what comes next.
Because while individuals can do well, together we achieve something extraordinary.
The Role
The Data Platform Engineer will ensure Norton Rose Fulbright’s enterprise data platform is a stable, secure and supportable IT service. The platform is built on Azure Databricks, Microsoft Fabric and associated Azure services, supports the firm's strategic data capability across EMEA and EMEAPAC, and is governed through Terraform, Azure DevOps and a standardised deployment framework.
The role is hands-on and service-focused. It provides the operational foundation needed to keep the platform reliable, observable, governed and ready for controlled production use. Its emphasis is on platform health, support processes, quality assurance, release readiness, incident response and continual service improvement.
The successful candidate will work closely with Architecture, Information Security, Service Delivery, Infrastructure, suppliers and consuming business teams to ensure  platform changes are deployed safely through established CI/CD processes, supported by appropriate monitoring, operational controls, documentation and governance standards.
Key Responsibilities
• Provide L2/L3 operational support for Microsoft Fabric, Azure Databricks, and associated Azure services.
• Maintain platform health, availability, resilience, and supportability across the data platform estate.
• Perform routine platform administration, operational checks, and capacity and utilisation monitoring.
• Monitor platform performance, identify optimisation opportunities, and maintain cost awareness.
• Troubleshoot issues across platform, identity, networking, storage, security, and integration layers.
• Manage incidents, problems, and service requests in line with established ITSM processes.
• Investigate and resolve operational issues, ensuring timely restoration of service.
• Support major incident response activities where platform services are impacted.
• Contribute to root cause analysis and implement actions to improve platform stability and reduce issue recurrence.
• Collaborate with internal teams, suppliers, and stakeholders to deliver effective operational support.
• Support change, release, and environment management activities across the platform estate.
• Maintain release readiness checklists and operational acceptance criteria.
• Validate platform changes prior to production deployment to ensure supportability and risk controls are in place.
• Support the management of Development, Test, and Production environments.
• Ensure configuration consistency across environments and platform services.
• Contribute to CI/CD, version control, and release automation practices for platform assets.
• Promote operational excellence through continuous improvement, knowledge sharing, and robust documentation.
Quality, Monitoring and Governance
A key part of the role is to define and execute operational QA checks for platform changes, integrations and supplier-delivered components. The engineer will verify that monitoring, alerting, logging, access controls, runbooks, escalation routes and support processes are in place before production release. They will support service acceptance and transition activity, assessing readiness against availability, recoverability, supportability, security and control requirements.
The role will implement and maintain monitoring, alerting and observability across Fabric, Databricks and Azure services. It will develop service health reporting, operational dashboards and exception monitoring, and maintain runbooks, known error records, support documentation and knowledge articles. The engineer will contribute to service reviews, operational assurance and continual improvement.
The role will support governance, security and compliance by assisting with access control, role management, privileged access processes, audit evidence, metadata, lineage, auditability and policy enforcement. It will work with Risk, Privacy, Information Security and Architecture to ensure platform operations remain aligned with NRF policies, approved architecture patterns and applicable control requirements.
Key Skills and Experience
• Experience supporting cloud-based data platforms in production or near-production environments, ideally including Microsoft Fabric, Azure Databricks, or both.
• Strong understanding of Azure services and operational dependencies, including workspaces, capacities, lakehouses, pipelines, clusters, jobs, Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, OneLake, Key Vault, Azure Monitor, Log Analytics, Entra ID, managed identities, secure networking, and private endpoint architectures.
• Proven experience in IT Service Management (ITSM), including incident, problem, change, release, and service request management.
• Experience working with ServiceNow or equivalent service management tools.
• Knowledge of production support models, escalation processes, service transition, and knowledge management practices.
• Ability to create and maintain runbooks, operational procedures, technical documentation, and support knowledge articles.
• Practical experience of quality assurance, release governance, and operational readiness activities.
• Experience validating technical changes, defining operational acceptance criteria, and managing Development, Test, and Production environments.
• Understanding of test and deployment evidence reviews, rollback planning, and identifying operational support gaps before go-live.
• Experience with monitoring, logging, diagnostics, dashboards, Azure DevOps, Git, CI/CD tooling, and automation.
• Working knowledge of scripting and infrastructure-as-code tools such as PowerShell, Python, and Terraform.
• Understanding of data platform governance, security controls, data classification, retention policies, privacy requirements, and audit processes…

SLR is a global leader in sustainability solutions, working with clients to help make sustainability happen, within a collaborative, people‑first culture.
Due to continued growth, we are seeking an experienced Mine Water Professional to join our established Mine Water team, delivering high‑profile integrated water management and mining sector projects.
Based in Edinburgh, Bristol, Nottingham, London or Dublin, the role will focus primarily on mine water management, hydrology and water resource engineering for local and international mining projects, with additional exposure to feasibility studies, due diligence, ESIA and closure planning, as well as a small amount of other multi‑disciplinary work spanning renewables, infrastructure, power, industrial and built‑environment sectors.

You’ll lead the delivery of mine water and hydrology projects from planning through to detailed design, working closely with clients and multidisciplinary teams. The role includes:
• Project and technical leadership – delivering integrated water management solutions across the mining lifecycle, including feasibility studies (PEA/PFS/FS), operational improvements, due diligence, ESIA and closure planning
• Client management and proposal support – enquiry handling, client liaison, technical workshops, reporting, QA/QC and site visits
• Mentoring and coaching less experienced engineers and scientists – supporting team capability, resource planning and strategic development
• Desk‑based work alongside site visits across the UK, Ireland, Europe and internationally – collaborating with colleagues across Europe, Asia‑Pacific, Africa and the Americas
You’ll collaborate with colleagues across Environmental and Earth Sciences, Planning, ESIA, Engineering and Global Advisory on complex and impactful mining projects, with opportunities for European and international exposure.
Rewards & Benefits
SLR’s ‘One Team’ culture is at the heart of our business, providing a collaborative and supportive environment for professional development. Through a structured career framework, regular performance reviews, and full support toward chartership, professional qualifications and licences, we offer outstanding opportunities for long‑term career progression.
Our flexible benefits & reward package includes:
• Competitive salary with discretionary bonus
• Company pension
• Private medical insurance
• Life, income, and travel insurance
• Salary sacrifice car lease and cycle‑to‑work schemes
We believe sustainable careers need balance, so we offer:
• Flexible, hybrid and agile working
• 25 days’ annual leave plus flexible public holidays
• Buy or sell leave options
• Core working hours
• Cross‑border remote working and sabbatical opportunities
Family life and wellbeing matter at SLR:
We provide enhanced maternity, paternity and adoption leave, access to an Employee Assistance Programme, and specialist support for mental health, stress and menopause—supporting our people both professionally and personally.
About You
You’ll bring:
• Extensive experience delivering mine water, hydrology or water resource projects, ideally within the mining sector
• A degree in hydrology, water resources engineering, environmental engineering, geology or a related field, with professional registration (CEng, CEnv or CSci)
• Project management and stakeholder engagement experience, including client liaison and technical workshop delivery

• Stormwater management and hydraulic design
• Flood hydrology and rainfall‑runoff modelling
• Water balance modelling and water resource management
• Planning and design of water management infrastructure
• Dam break assessment for water and tailings storage facilities
Desirable additional experience:
• Field hydrology programme design and execution
• Water quality monitoring and modelling
• GoldSim probabilistic scenario modelling
• Newtonian and non‑Newtonian hydraulic modelling
• Data management, data science, GIS and/or CAD
• Cost estimation and design specifications
• Water treatment plant and pumping system design
Culture & Inclusion

We are committed to equal opportunities and foster a workplace where everyone can thrive, supported by active Culture & Inclusion Committees and Employee Networks. We welcome applications from candidates of all backgrounds and are a Disability Confident Committed employer. takeaway.wd3.myworkdayjobs.com/jet-ecs-r.description_excerpt:
Ready for a challenge?
Then Just Eat Takeaway.com might be the place for you. We’re a leading global online delivery platform, and our vision is to empower everyday convenience.
Whether it’s a Friday-night feast, a post-gym poke bowl, or grabbing some groceries, our tech platform connects tens of millions of customers with hundreds of thousands of restaurant, grocery and convenience partners across the globe.
About this role
Our logistics network spans 16 markets, hundreds of thousands of couriers and more than 350 million orders a year. Behind every order are real-time decisions: who delivers it, when, and at what price. Models running in production make them.
We are looking for a Director of Data Science & Machine Learning to lead the function behind those decisions and take the optimisation of our network to the next level. This is a leader-of-leaders role: a global team of 90+ data scientists, operations research scientists, ML engineers and MLOps engineers, led through managers and principal data scientists. You will set the DS/OR/ML agenda, not just run it.
The challenge is dual: keeping the real-time decision systems reliable at marketplace scale, while pushing the frontier on optimisation, supply/demand shaping and applied AI.
Location: Hybrid, 3 days a week from our London or Amsterdam office and 2 days working from home
These are some of the key components to the position:
• Deliver measurable improvement in delivery time, courier utilisation, cost per order, and the efficiency of courier pay.
• Own the strategy and roadmap for real-time decision systems: demand forecasting and supply balancing, order-to-courier assignment, and dynamic pay and fee pricing. All running as low latency production services at marketplace scale.
• Understand and shape courier behaviour: lead incentive and pay design grounded in economics and causal modelling, anticipating how couriers respond to the levers we pull
• Set the Operations Research agenda: combinatorial optimisation, exact and heuristic solvers, and simulation for capacity planning and policy testing
• Set the bar for validation before launch: backtesting and simulation frameworks that gate models going into production
• Own the quality of the ML platform and MLOps standards: feature and model pipelines, CI/CD, online and batch serving, monitoring and drift detection
• Drive experimentation and causal inference in a marketplace, including switchback and geo-based designs where network effects break standard A/B tests, and connect short-term experiment results to long-term outcomes such as courier retention and network health
• Build applied AI that delivers value in production, including LLM-based and agentic products for couriers and operations
• Build the organisation: hire, develop managers and principals, and build university partnerships
• Partner with Logistics Product, Logistics Engineering, Commercial and central Technology on production delivery of dispatch, estimations, pay, and supply/demand shaping actions, aligning on priorities and outcomes
What will you bring to the team?
• Leadership experience in Data Science, ML or Operations Research, including significant experience leading large organisations through managers across time zones, and developing those managers
• Deep credibility in real-time ML and marketplace or network optimisation (logistics, ride-hailing, delivery or similar)
• Experience taking models from research into low-latency production at scale
• Strong grounding in experimentation and causal inference under network effects, and in the economics of multi-sided marketplaces where participants respond strategically
• Excellent stakeholder management and communication, able to influence at the Product and Engineering leadership table and translate technical choices into business outcomes
• A pragmatic approach to AI: you ship value, not demos
• Advanced degree in a quantitative field (or equivalent experience)
At JET, this is how we play
Our teams forge connections internally and work with some of the best-known brands on the planet, giving us truly international impact in a dynamic environment.
Being the best at what we do isn’t just about delivering on our strategy. It's a competition for something incredibly valuable – our customers' choice. Every time a customer decides where to order, they're picking a side.
At the heart of the JET Customer League are our values and behaviours. They guide every interaction, every decision, every innovation. These are the actions we need to perform consistently and brilliantly, to surpass the competition and earn our customers’ loyalty, again and again.
Fun, fast-paced and supportive, the JET culture is about movement, growth, helping one another to succeed and celebrating wins. By truly living our values and embodying our behaviours, we’re building a customer-first culture which enables us to stay one step ahead of the competition.
Inclusion, Diversity & Belonging
No matter who you are, what you look like, who you love, or where you are from, you can find your place at Just Eat Takeaway.com. We’re committed to creating an inclusive culture, encouraging diversity of people and thinking, in which all employees feel they truly belong and can bring their most colourful selves to work every day.
What else are we delivering?
Want to know more about our JETers, culture or company? Have a look at our career site where you can find people's stories, blogs, podcasts and more JET journeys.

In addition, we’re proud to host an onsite restaurant that shares our commitment to sustainability by providing delicious seasonal menus which have been created with the planet in mind. Finally, your physical wellness is well-catered for with our onsite gym facilities and medical centre.
Roles Description
This role is a client facing role and sits within the Global Markets Agreements and Documentation. The candidate is responsible for drafting, negotiation, advising and execution of trading documentation on behalf of Bank of America entities. In this role, you will be working on complex, high impact documentation that directly supports global clients. You will play a key part in enabling efficient client onboarding, supporting business growth and ensuring compliance with regulatory and internal standards, while gaining broad exposure across products and stakeholders.
You will act as a relationship manager for a portfolio of priority Markets clients, serving as the primary point of contact for documentation negotiations across Markets agreement suite. In doing so, you will build trusted relationships and become a go-to advisor for clients navigating documentation requirements. You will develop a close partnership with Sales, Onboarding and other internal stakeholders, giving you a highly visible position within the business and a clear line of sight into how commercial and credit decisions are executed through documentation. Your work will ensure agreements accurately reflect agreed commercial and credit terms while meeting regulatory and policy requirements.
Key responsibilities
• Negotiate, draft, structure and advice  on a wide range of derivatives documentation including ISDA Master Agreements, Credit Support Annexes, IM documentation and bespoke Collateral agreements; cleared derivatives documentation; GMRA and GMSLA; FBF and Deutscher Rahmenvertrag  on behalf of various Bank of America entities.
• Work closely with Sales, Credit and the Onboarding team to maximize the efficiency of the documentation onboarding of clients.
• Advise front office, sales and trading, operations risk and collateral on documentation issues arising during negotiations
• Act as Relationship Manager for the suite of agreements for a portfolio of high priority clients, serving as the primary point of contact and coordinating the agreement negotiation process across products.
• Liaise with internal partners and marketers/traders to accurately reflect the necessary credit and business terms in the transactional suite while ensuring compliance with applicable laws and regulations and bank guidelines and policies.
• Update trading agreement and other systems of record.
• Work on regulatory and other special projects as and when required.
Required Qualifications
• Prior related experience in a similar role
• Strong substantive knowledge of markets documentation (French law and/or German law master agreements)
• Language skills: German and/or French
• Excellent communication, analytical and organisational skills.
• Ability to work independently while being part of a cohesive team.
• Highly self-motivated with the ability to prioritize and drive execution.
• Ability to exercise excellent judgment within defined parameters.
• Significant experience with hedge fund structures and the PB industry.
• Law qualified preferred but not necessary.
Benefits of working at Bank of America (UK):

Job role
The Sales Director leads the sales strategy, execution, and performance across the assigned Material Science sub-industry/application in EMEA. This role translates product basket and portfolio strategies into account-specific sales plans, pricing execution, and pipeline growth. The Sales Director partners closely with IMM, Product Management, Supply Chain, Operations, and Technical teams to drive revenue, GP margin, and customer value through solution-selling and market activation. The position is central to developing market insights, identifying growth opportunities, and supporting Material Science’s long-term strategic direction.
Essential Responsibilities and Tasks
Sales Strategy, Account Leadership, and Pipeline Management (50%)
• Translate product baskets and portfolio guidance into regional sales plans with clear revenue, GP margin, and share-of-wallet targets.
• Define priority customer segments and target accounts; lead account planning, territory design, and coverage models.
• Build and manage a healthy opportunity pipeline; drive opportunity qualification, stage progression, and conversion rates.
• Lead sales teams to push revenue and profit growth across targeted product baskets and identify customer demands beyond existing product portfolio
• Collaborate with operations and supply chain teams to drive efficiency and productivity.
• Ensure CRM discipline, forecast accuracy, and sales performance governance; run monthly/quarterly business reviews.
• Coordinate with Account Managers and Sales Managers to execute strategic campaigns, new product introductions, and customer value propositions.
• Cultivate senior-level relationships at key customers; act as a trusted advisor representing Brenntag’s technical and commercial capabilities.
• Identify risks (resource constraints, market shifts, competitive moves) and implement mitigation plans for sales execution.
Industry/Application Know-How and Market Activation (30%)
• Develop deep market and application expertise to co-create strategies with IMM aligned to the Material Science Industry Market Management framework.
• Identify trends and technologies with commercial potential, define priority segments and growth areas, and convert insights into actionable sales plays and strategic narratives
• Spot portfolio gaps and align with Industry Market Management to ensure strategic coverage and market relevance.
• Define themes and priorities for trade fairs, webinars, and customer events; represent Material Science at regional exhibitions and customer meetings and events.
• Activate campaigns and technical storytelling to support the sales organization and accelerate adoption of new solutions.
• Monitor portfolio balance and alignment with internal stakeholders to avoid conflicts and ensure compliance with regulatory and quality requirements.
Pricing Execution and Margin Management (20%)
• Implement pricing guidance derived from IMM’s market intelligence and supplier input
• Maintain accurate pricing information in relevant systems; monitor price/mix development and drive margin optimization initiatives.
• Provide feedback loops to IMM and Product Management on competitive dynamics, customer willingness-to-pay, and price realization.
• Coordinate with Product Management on supply agreements and execution; ensure sales commitments align with sourcing strategies.
Education and Experience
• University degree in a relevant field (Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, Business, or similar).
• Extensive experience in specialty chemical distribution or manufacturing, with significant leadership in sales and commercial management.
• Strong technical and commercial knowledge in Material Science applications (e.g., polymers, coatings, adhesives, sealants, elastomers, construction chemicals, composites, additives).
• Experience collaborating with Product Management, Procurement, or Application Development; familiarity with VAS solution-selling is preferred.
Key Performance Indicators
• Revenue growth and GP margin improvement versus plan.
• Pipeline health (coverage, stage distribution) and conversion rates.
• Forecast accuracy and CRM data quality.
• Share-of-wallet expansion within priority accounts.
• VAS attach rate and cross-selling across the portfolio.
Travel
Up to 50% travel required, depending on customer visits, supplier meetings, internal sessions, and project needs.

• Support content governance and review cycles to ensure records remain current, accurate, appropriately owned, and reviewed within established timelines — leading large-scale quarterly updates and identifying outdated, duplicative, or underutilized content for remediation.

• Identify and apply opportunities to use AI and other available technology in day-to-day content management work to improve efficiency, quality, and consistency.

They play a pivotal role in enabling the innovation that powers some of the world's most advanced aerospace and industrial technologies. This is an opportunity to take ownership of a diverse pilot plant environment, working at the intersection of engineering excellence and research and development.
As a Maintenance Engineer at our Leicester site, you will enjoy:
• Autonomy and Ownership: Supporting the site's maintenance strategy, driving reliability, performance, and continuous improvement initiatives.
• A Unique Engineering Environment: Working with cutting-edge pilot plant equipment that underpins the development of next-generation composite materials and manufacturing technologies.
• Visible Impact: Collaborating with our R&D team where your maintenance expertise will impact site productivity and innovation.
With our strong investment in research and development and our culture of continuous improvement, Hexcel is the industry leader in the manufacturing of advanced lightweight composite materials, including carbon fibre, woven reinforcements, resins, prepregs, honeycombs, engineered core and composite structures. We invite you to join the Hexcel team at our Leicester site and become part of the "strength within."
Key Responsibilities
• Own and manage the Planned Preventative Maintenance (PPM) programme to maximise equipment reliability, availability, and operational performance.
• Develop, implement, and continuously improve maintenance schedules and maintenance strategies across the pilot plant.
• Provide hands-on technical support for equipment breakdowns, diagnosing faults and coordinating effective repairs to minimise downtime.
• Ensure maintenance activities comply with company procedures, engineering best practice, safety requirements, and relevant legislation.
• Collaborate with the R&D Technical Manager and operational teams to schedule maintenance activities with minimal disruption.
• Lead root cause investigations and implement corrective actions to improve equipment reliability and maintenance effectiveness.
• Manage external contractors and service providers, ensuring safe working practices and delivery to agreed standards.
• Control spare parts and maintenance inventory, mitigating risk and ensuring critical parts availability.
• Maintain accurate maintenance records, reports, and documentation to support compliance and continuous improvement.
• Champion a strong safety culture, ensuring safe isolation procedures, contractor compliance, and adherence to site safety standards.
What We're Looking For
• Proven experience in a Maintenance Engineer, Reliability Engineer, or similar engineering role within manufacturing, process, industrial, R&D, or engineering environments.
• Mechanical, electrical, or multi-skilled engineering expertise with strong technical fault-finding and diagnostic capability.
• Experience managing Planned Preventative Maintenance (PPM) systems and maintenance planning activities.
• Strong understanding of health and safety regulations and engineering best practices within an industrial environment.
• Experience coordinating contractors, suppliers, and external service providers.
• Demonstrated ability to investigate equipment issues, identify root causes, and implement sustainable solutions.
• Strong organisational and planning skills with the ability to manage competing priorities effectively.
• Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills with the ability to build effective cross-functional relationships.
• Proactive, hands-on approach with a strong sense of ownership and accountability.
• HNC/HND (or equivalent) in Mechanical, Electrical, or a related Engineering discipline. Knowledge of PUWER, LOLER, and HSE regulations is desirable, alongside an engineering apprenticeship background.
Why Join Hexcel?
This is more than a maintenance role. It is an opportunity to become the engineering owner of a critical pilot plant environment, influencing how reliability and safety are delivered. You'll work alongside talented technical R&D specialists, contribute directly to innovative product development activities, and help ensure the equipment and infrastructure supporting Hexcel's future remains at the highest standard.
