kla.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com/search/job/new.description_excerpt:
To make electronics, you need chips, wafers, transistors, reticles, and... To make these, you must see, test and manufacture them at scale—faster and better than ever before. That's where KLA comes in. Whether you're early in your career or an experienced professional, you'll solve complex challenges, work alongside brilliant minds and help shape the future of technology.
Group/Division
The Semiconductor Products and Customers (Semi PC) business unit designs, builds and sells KLA’s product portfolio to help chip manufacturers meet high-quality standards for technologies like AI, data centers, automotive and electronic devices. Our inspection, metrology, and analytics systems detect and monitor defects across logic and memory chips, specialty semiconductors, wafers, reticles, advanced packaging, process equipment and materials. We also develop technologies for specialty processes, IC substrates, and PCB manufacturing, including etch and deposition, component inspection, and imaging and analytics. The SPTS division provides advanced wafer processing solutions—including etch, deposition and vapor-based technologies—designed for R&D through high-volume production. With a global presence and strong customer support network, SPTS helps manufacturers across industries improve performance, yield and cost-efficiency. It also offers comprehensive service and spare parts through a worldwide network of service centers and qualified local agents.
What You'll Do
In this role, you will play a key part in advancing business priorities by delivering high-impact work across your area of expertise.
As part of the plasma dicing team, the primary responsibilities of this position include developing plasma etch processes, processing customer wafers using etch demonstration equipment, and documenting the completed sample processing activities.
Additional responsibilities include providing customer technical support, preparing technical reports for internal and external stakeholders, generating intellectual property submissions, and supporting other business units as required.
Key Responsibilities
Process Demonstrations
• Develop and demonstrate plasma etch processes to meet agreed specifications.
• Assess results using analytical equipment and relevant software tools.
• Perform process troubleshooting and root cause analysis.
• Provide regular updates to Product Management on demonstration and sample work.
• Build and maintain effective relationships with customers and the global KLA support network.
• Summarise findings through technical reports and presentations.
Process Development
• Develop and optimise processes across SPTS product platforms.
• Plan and execute work safely, efficiently, and to agreed timescales.
• Utilise endpoint detection techniques to enhance process control and performance.
• Conduct long-duration testing for new processes and equipment.
• Contribute to cross-functional projects supporting new products and technologies.
• Prepare technical reports to support patent applications, publications, and conferences.
Field Support
• Develop and optimise SPTS processes to meet customer requirements at customer sites.
• Provide factory-based technical support to field teams and customers.
• Establish and maintain strong customer relationships through effective technical support.
Qualifications and Experience
The successful candidate will have:
• Master's degree, or Bachelor's degree in a relevant discipline, together with relevant industrial experience. Candidates with equivalent qualifications and hands-on semiconductor process engineering experience are also encouraged to apply
• Experience of plasma etch processing within a semiconductor environment.
• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
• Experience with semiconductor metrology techniques.
• SEM experience would be advantageous, although training can be provided.
• Knowledge and practical experience of endpoint detection techniques.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills.
• The ability to work both independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team.
• Excellent organisational and time-management skills.
What We Offer
• 25 days annual leave plus bank holidays
• Share scheme
• Contributory pension scheme
• Cash health plan
• Cycle to Work scheme
• Global bonus plan
• Employee rewards scheme
• Life assurance
Occasional domestic and international travel, including to the United States, may be required as part of this role to support customer installations and development activities. Occasional shift work may also be required. Certain roles at KLA may require permits, licenses or other approvals to access specific technologies, systems or information, and obtaining such approvals may form part of the assessment process for the role.
Minimum Qualifications
About KLA
We provide advanced inspection tools, metrology systems, process solutions, and computational analytics that make electronics possible, tackling complex challenges. From electron and photon optics to machine learning and data analytics, we seek perfection at the most fundamental level of matter in the universe. If you want to make electronics that push industries forward and make the world a better place, join us.
Use of AI Statement
At KLA, our interviews seek to understand your individual skills, problem-solving approach and authentic thinking. To ensure a fair and consistent evaluation, the use of AI, recording tools or other technologies to generate, suggest or provide responses during interviews—whether virtual or in person—is not permitted unless explicitly approved in advance as part of a reasonable accommodation or invited by the interviewer. Use of these tools may interfere with our ability to evaluate your individual qualifications and affect your candidacy. KLA is committed to advancing innovation through responsible AI, and we value candidates who share this mindset.
We offer a competitive, family friendly total rewards package. We design our programs to reflect our commitment to an inclusive environment, while ensuring we provide benefits that meet the diverse needs of our employees.
KLA is proud to be an equal opportunity employer.

Personal Qualities

• Passionate about technology and innovation, with impeccable attention to detail

• Calm, effective and flexible under pressure during live operational events and project deadlines

• Significant experience supporting and delivering enterprise-scale AV systems in commercial and/or corporate environments

AtkinsRéalis is a world-class engineering services and nuclear organisation delivering complex and critical programmes across defence, aerospace, nuclear and other highly regulated sectors.

• A relevant degree, maritime qualification or equivalent experience gained in defence, the Armed Forces or industry.
Desirable experience
• Knowledge of Defence Maritime Regulations, DSA02-DMR, JSP 815 or Naval Authority arrangements.
• Experience supporting platform certification, safety-case quality control or naval safety management systems.
• Knowledge of relevant functional-safety, maritime and naval standards.
• Professional registration, or active progress towards IEng or CEng, and membership of a relevant institution such as the IET, SaRS, IMechE, IExpE or RAeS.

Job Description
Mechanical Design Engineer
Location: New Mills, Wotton-under-Edge, South Gloucestershire
up to £38,000 depending on experience
Renishaw's Machine Tool Products Division is a world leader in the design, development, and manufacture of inspection probe technology and metrology systems for precision-machined components. We are seeking a Mechanical Design Engineer to join our Mechanical Design Team at our global headquarters in South Gloucestershire.
Our design team is responsible for transforming product requirements into robust, validated engineering solutions. Working closely with cross-functional teams, we balance performance, manufacturability, cost, quality, and sustainability considerations to deliver innovative products that meet the needs of our customers and the business. The successful candidate will contribute to the development of new machine tool probes, interfaces, sensors, and early-stage research activities.
The Role
As a Mechanical Design Engineer, you will:
• Translate product requirements into innovative concepts and production-ready designs.
• Produce supporting engineering calculations, analyses, and technical documentation.
• Create, manage, and control 3D models, assemblies, Bills of Materials (BOMs), and detailed drawings.
• Apply sound engineering principles to develop robust and reliable design solutions.
• Collaborate with manufacturing, quality, procurement, and other engineering disciplines to ensure designs are optimised for manufacture and assembly (DFM/DFA).
• Support New Product Introduction (NPI) activities and design effective production assembly tooling.
• Contribute to design simplification, standardisation, and cost reduction through value engineering principles.
• Participate in product verification reviews to ensure designs meet performance and reliability requirements. Support the product development team developing targeted test strategies.
Key Requirements
• A practical, hands-on approach to engineering and problem-solving.
• A positive attitude, strong work ethic, and willingness to learn.
• Degree qualification in Mechanical Engineering or a related discipline. Other qualifications will be considered including HND when supported by proven experience.
• Good understanding of mechanical engineering fundamentals.
• Awareness of engineering materials, their properties, and appropriate applications.
• Experience using 3D CAD software to create and manage parts, assemblies, BOMs, and detailed drawings (Siemens NX preferred).
• Ability to work effectively within a multi-disciplinary engineering team.
• Understanding of Finite Element Analysis (FEA) and its application to engineering problems.
• Understanding of the relationship between product design, manufacturing processes, and assembly.
Desirable Requirements
• Experience within a mechanical product design environment.
• Knowledge of industrial measurement and their applications.
• Understanding of the product development lifecycle and New Product Introduction processes.
• Good knowledge of mechanical fundamentals, including free body diagrams, statics, bending, and torsion theory.
• Experience creating and interpreting Finite Element Analysis models and results (ANSYS preferred).
• Understanding of materials including stainless steels, heat-treated ferrous materials, aluminium alloys, cermet’s, ceramics and injection moulding.
• Demonstrated problem-solving skills with the ability to identify root causes and implement effective solutions.
• Ability to build strong working relationships and collaborate across different functions within the business.
We are looking for someone with strong engineering fundamentals, curiosity, and a desire to develop their technical expertise. If you do not meet every requirement but have a positive attitude, practical engineering aptitude, and a willingness to learn, we would still encourage you to apply.
Benefits
When you join Renishaw, we're committing to your future career. That's because we believe in developing our people's skills and promoting them internally. We also offer a benefits package that's highly desirable; including a 9% non-contributory pension, discretionary annual bonus, *subsidised onsite restaurants and *coffee shops, free parking, *car sharing scheme and *24 hour fitness centres. ( not available at all sites).
We also want to promote a healthy work-life balance as much as possible, so we have introduced a hybrid working policy which allows for a combination of home and office based working depending on the nature of your role. We also offer a variable working programme, 25 days holiday plus bank holidays, Life Assurance policy of 12 times annual salary, Cycle to Work scheme, enhanced maternity pay subject to qualifying criteria, Health Cash Plan, the option to join Renishaw Health Trust (Aviva) and an Employee Assistance Programme for employees and family.

The Role:
Joining Moderna means advancing mRNA science to transform medicine. Work with exceptional global teams on a broad pipeline and build a career that makes a real difference for patients.
Moderna is strengthening its presence in Harwell, a globally recognised centre for scientific research and innovation. Our Harwell team is expanding the bioanalytical capabilities that support our growing mRNA pipeline, bringing together exceptional scientists to advance transformative medicines for patients around the world.
As a Scientist within the Bioanalytical and Molecular Assays team, you will play a pivotal role in advancing Moderna's clinical development programmes by designing and delivering innovative immunogenicity and bioanalytical strategies. Working closely with multidisciplinary teams across research, bioanalysis and clinical development, you will help generate the high-quality data that accelerates novel mRNA-derived therapeutics from discovery into the clinic while contributing to future pipeline innovation.
This is an exciting opportunity to combine scientific expertise with cutting-edge technologies in a highly collaborative environment. Alongside developing robust bioanalytical capabilities, you will have opportunities to leverage emerging digital technologies and Generative AI-enabled tools that continue to transform scientific workflows, data interpretation and decision-making across Moderna's research organisation.
Here's What You'll Do:
•
Design and execute phase-appropriate bioanalytical strategies supporting regulated clinical programmes.
•
Lead the development of immunogenicity assays, including anti-drug antibody (ADA) and neutralising antibody (nAb) assays, alongside pharmacokinetic (PK) and pharmacodynamic (PD) assays for therapeutic protein quantitation.
•
Ensure bioanalytical assays are developed, qualified and validated in line with programme timelines and applicable regulatory expectations.
•
Develop and optimise assays using ELISA, MSD, cell culture, immunoblotting and other relevant bioanalytical technologies.
•
Help establish and expand Moderna's internal bioanalytical capabilities to support the growing mRNA portfolio.
•
Procure, qualify and maintain analytical laboratory equipment while preparing and maintaining Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
•
Determine, qualify and control critical assay reagents to support robust and reproducible assay performance.
•
Partner closely with Preclinical, Clinical Operations and Sample Management teams to define sample journeys and develop laboratory manuals supporting regulated studies.
•
Troubleshoot scientific and technical issues that arise during assay development and regulated bioanalytical activities.
•
Communicate scientific concepts, experimental findings, programme objectives and data analyses effectively within a highly matrixed global environment.
•
Contribute to the integration of basic science research, bioanalysis and informatics to advance programmes into clinical development while helping translate clinical findings into future opportunities across Moderna's pipeline.
Here's What You'll Bring to the Table:
•
PhD with at least three years of relevant experience, or an MSc with five or more years of hands-on experience in bioanalytical method development, validation and sample analysis. Equivalent combinations of education, technical training and relevant laboratory experience will also be considered.
•
Strong knowledge of Good Clinical Practice (GCP) requirements together with an understanding of current regulatory expectations and industry trends within bioanalytical science.
•
Expert knowledge of bioanalytical assay platforms including electrochemiluminescence (ECL), immunoassays, cell culture-based assays and related clinical assay methodologies.
•
Hands-on experience with cell culture assays is advantageous.
•
Experience working with RNA therapeutics, biologics and/or cell therapies is preferred.
•
Working knowledge of translational science and the evolving competitive landscape within the mRNA field.
•
Curiosity, adaptability and a willingness to learn new scientific concepts while challenging conventional thinking.
•
Excellent attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple projects within a fast-paced research environment.
•
Experience using Laboratory Information Management Systems (LIMS) and electronic laboratory notebook (eLNB) platforms is preferred.
•
Knowledge of FDA, MHRA and global regulatory data standards.
•
Excellent communication skills with the ability to explain scientific concepts, programme objectives and data analyses across multidisciplinary teams.
•

• Lead high-profile policy initiatives across the UK asset management and funds sector, helping shape regulation that delivers better outcomes for consumers, firms and markets

• Stay ahead of market developments, emerging business models and global regulatory change, helping the FCA respond to a rapidly evolving environment
• Build trusted relationships across industry, government, consumer groups and regulatory partners, bringing diverse perspectives into policy development
• Work collaboratively across the FCA and represent the organization externally, shaping discussions and delivering effective policy implementation
• Support and develop colleagues while strengthening your own leadership, regulatory and policy expertise in a role with significant visibility and reach across UK financial services

• Prior experience in public policy, financial regulation, legal or regulatory analysis, with a good understanding of the investment funds and asset management sector and its regulatory landscape

Essential:
• Good knowledge of UK and international funds regulation and the institutional frameworks that shape the asset management sector
• Experience contributing to policy development, regulatory change, consultations, rulemaking or impact assessments
• Demonstrated ability to lead complex workstreams, manage competing priorities and deliver high-quality outputs to deadline
• Effective stakeholder management and influencing skills, with the ability to build credibility with senior internal and external stakeholders

Medivet Old Isleworth is a cherished part of the local community, boasting a thriving client base that has grown organically through word of mouth.
We are currently looking for an experience Head Veterinary Nurse to join our close-knit team.
As a small animal first opinion practice, we pride ourselves on our loyal clients and our skilled Registered Veterinary Nurses and receptionists, who handle a diverse caseload. Our vibrant and dedicated team strives for excellence and embraces a culture of continuous learning while going the extra mile for our patients.
Our practice is well-equipped, featuring digital x-ray, ultrasound, and a full lab with a microscope, urinalysis machine, haematology, and biochemistry analyser. All out-of-hours care is managed by a nearby Medivet hospital in Richmond, where you’ll also have access to CT and MRI services. Located on a picturesque high street, our practice enjoys a delightful village atmosphere.
This permanent role is full-time at 40 hours per week and will include some weekends at the prestigious, flagship hospital, Richmond.
If you’re passionate about veterinary care and want to be part of a supportive team, we’d love to hear from you!
If you would like more information, for a friendly, initial conversation please contact joanne.gray@medivet.co.uk.
Responsibilities
Client care:
•
Deliver exceptional care to clients, each and every day.
Patient care:
•
Support the vet with any operations or procedures when required.
•
Carry out nurse led appointments.
•
Responsible for patient monitoring and care.
•
Manage admissions and discharges for procedures as directed by the Vet or Lead Vet (depending on complexity).
•
Ensure patient records are accurate and up to date.
•
Ensure all pre or post operation activity is completed.
•
Provide everyday care for patients by carrying out appropriate walking, toileting and feeding.
•
Complete any patient transfers required to out of hours (OOH) care provider or for any enhanced care required.
•
Responsible for dispensing and checking any medication required.
•
All patient care is carried out under the guidance of the Vet/Lead Vet in line with clinical competence.
Standards and Compliance:
•
Accountable for clinical compliance with all regulatory and practice standards and agreed ways of working.
•
Ensure the appropriate regulatory, practice and operational veterinary and nursing standards are implemented in the practice.
•
Ensure compliance with health and safety requirements.
Communications:
•
Hold daily briefings and co-ordinate roles and activity to support the effective running of the clinic.
•
Effectively deliver timely clinical communications to veterinary and nursing teams sharing news of changes or improvements to processes or practice standards, Social Ecosystem Model (SEM) outcomes etc.
•
Carry out engaging clinical meetings with the nursing team.
Clinical leadership:
•
Support and carry out clinical coaching as required.
•
Pro-actively share clinical best practice within and across clinics and the wider Medivet community.
•
Responsible for training and the development of the nursing team.
•
Ensure the clinical team are clear on their responsibilities and any tasks that need to be completed each day.
•
Ensure that Veterinary Nurses have appropriate clinical support and coaching.
•
Lead, manage and promote nurse led appointments and Schedule 3 surgeries.
•
To continue to deliver exceptional care to clients the Vet and Lead Vet are responsible for mentoring graduates within the clinic. The Nurse and Head Nurse are responsible for coaching the nursing team.
Clinical administration:
•
Take samples as required by and under the direction of the Vet/Lead Vet.
•
Ensure lab tests are carried out correctly.
•
Effectively manage the stock in the clinic and place any orders required.
•
Escalate any issues to the Practice Manager and/or Vet/Lead Vet as required.
•
Ensure the back of house is set up and ready for procedures.
Skills, knowledge and experience
•
Must be an RCVS registered nurse.
•
Able to confidently lead a clinical team.
•
Effective planning and management of the clinical team.
•
Implementation of a progressive clinical culture through nurse clinics and nurse consultations.
•
Supports nurse consults and understands how this contributes to the performance and efficient operation of the clinic.
•
Able to work as part of a team.
•
Able to deliver exceptional care to clients.
•
Experienced in using coaching and influencing skills to get the best out of each and every colleague
Our clinics are run by small teams who need to work together effectively to deliver exceptional care to our clients, patients, and colleagues. This means that, from time to time, you may be required to carry out tasks outside your normal duties, where you have the skills, knowledge and experience required.

unitedliving.wd502.myworkdayjobs.com/uni.description_excerpt:
United Infrastructure is a dynamic and rapidly expanding business, focused on delivering critical infrastructure projects, across the utility and social infrastructure sectors.
Our team of highly skilled and hardworking specialists deliver innovative solutions to the complex challenges our clients face.
Our company is split into two business areas:
Utility Infrastructure –
Our team of Utility Infrastructure specialists design, build and maintain critical water, energy (gas), power and telecoms infrastructure, for the UK’s largest network owners and operators.
Social Infrastructure -
Our team of Social Infrastructure specialists revitalise homes and communities by carrying out a wide range of work, from retrofit to refurbishment, and maintenance.
Equal Opportunities Statement - At United Infrastructure, we are committed to making every interaction a positive and inclusive experience. If there is anything we can do to support you, remove barriers, or make the process more accessible, please let us know — we want this to be the best possible experience for you.
We're looking for an experienced Marketing Manager to support our Energy and Water business. This is a varied, hands-on role where you'll take ownership of delivering marketing activity across the year, working closely with colleagues across the business to help raise our profile, support business development and tell the stories behind the work we do.
This is an exciting time for the world of energy as we look for renewable energy sources and United Infrastructure is at the forefront of the first carbon capture and storage project, in Liverpool Bay. This is a pivotal role liaising with stakeholders, media, government and local communities to communicate the future benefits of these projects are in line with our net zero commitments as a country.
You will be working closely with the Managing Directors of this business area to ensure that messaging is aligned to strategy throughout so being organised, confident and a good communicator is key.
No two days will be the same. One day you could be organising an industry exhibition, the next writing a press release, filming content on site or pulling together an award submission. We're looking for someone who enjoys getting stuck in, has plenty of ideas and is equally comfortable planning campaigns as they are delivering them.
Key Responsibilities
•
Manage and deliver the marketing programme across the Energy and Water divisions.
•
Plan and coordinate our annual events calendar, including exhibitions, conferences and stakeholder events.
•
Organise external events, manage delegate registrations and coordinate event logistics.
•
Manage exhibition branding, promotional merchandise and marketing materials.
•
Monitor marketing budgets, track costs and produce monthly spend reports.
•
Write and distribute press releases.
•
Produce case studies that showcase projects, people and business successes.
•
Work with colleagues across the business to develop thought leadership content and identify opportunities for articles, interviews and speaking events.
•
Research, write and submit entries for industry awards.
•
Create engaging content for LinkedIn and other social media channels.
•
Visit project sites to capture photos and video content for marketing campaigns.
•
Draft LinkedIn posts and edit short-form videos, including Reels for TikTok.
•
Help develop and produce podcasts using our in-house recording studio.
•
Support colleagues at exhibitions and events, ensuring our branding and marketing materials are presented professionally.
•
Travel to events, project sites and other business locations as required.
About You
You'll be someone who enjoys building relationships, can manage several projects at once and has a real passion for marketing. You'll be confident working with people across the business and happy to take ownership of your workload.
You'll ideally have:
•
Previous experience in a marketing role, ideally at Marketing Manager level.
•
Strong organisational and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities.
•
Excellent written communication skills with experience writing press releases, case studies and social media content.
•
Experience planning and delivering events.
•
Budget management experience.
•
A good eye for detail and an understanding of brand consistency.
•
Experience creating digital content for social media.
•
Confidence using photography and video equipment, or a willingness to learn.
•
Experience editing short-form video content.
•
A full UK driving licence.
It would be an advantage if you have:
•
Experience working in the energy, water, utilities or infrastructure sectors.
•
An understanding of the UK energy or water industries.
•
Experience producing podcasts or multimedia content.
•
Experience writing successful award submissions & engaging PR content.
Why Join Us?
This is a great opportunity to shape the marketing activity for two growing parts of the business. You'll have the freedom to bring new ideas, work on a wide variety of projects and play an important role in helping us promote the work we're doing across the Energy and Water sectors.
Join us at United Infrastructure and be part of our mission to deliver innovative and sustainable solutions to the complex infrastructure needs of the UK.

chaucergroup.wd3.myworkdayjobs.com/chauc.description_excerpt:
Job summary
This role is primarily responsible for helping the management of Chaucer’s capital both at a group level and an underlying subsidiary level. This includes helping on the following: formulating the capital policy; the related risk framework; the dividend strategy; debt equity composition strategy; corporate structure planning; underwriting entity available capital plans and then the execution and oversight of said strategies. All capital management related reporting to boards, Finance & Investment Committee, Exec Team, regulators, parent company and other stakeholders is included in the remit.
Main duties
Capital Management Execution
•
To assist the Deputy Head of Capital Management on the annual capital planning reporting and approval exercise with China Re.
•
To run the quarterly and annual capital rebalancing and profit distribution exercises with Lloyd’s for the Chaucer Syndicates.
•
To run any capital rebalancing exercises for the Irish underwriting entity.
•
To assist or run the execution of any debt structures, be it tier 1 or tier 2 solutions, liaising with lawyers and banks.
•
To own the execution as required on any capital restructuring per the agreed capital strategy.
Capital Reporting
•
To own production of all capital reporting to Group Head of Investments & Treasury.
•
To own all capital related MI reporting including to the following stakeholders: CFO, Exec Team, Finance & Investment Committee, Boards.
•
To own all capital related reporting to China Re including all regular reporting and ad-hoc request.
•
To own all regulatory and statutory capital related reporting including Lloyd’s returns, group financial statements, local returns.
•
To own all the submissions to rating agencies.
•
To own all return on capital reporting and analysis.
Capital Management Strategy
•
To help produce the Capital Policy, with the related risk framework, and submission for approval from the relevant Committees and Boards.
•
To work with the Deputy Head of Capital Management and Group Head of Investments & Treasury on formulating and analysing optimal capital structures for the Group and subsidiaries within.
•
To help create a longer-term capital management plan for the Group including equity from parent and debt.
•
To help create a capital plan for the underwriting entities: For the Lloyd’s of London business understanding and planning for the Lloyd’s capital cycle and for the Irish business understanding the rating agency and CBI requirements.
•
To help formulate the dividend policy to parent, working closely with China Re, Capital Modelling, Tax and Finance.
•
To work closely with the Group Head of I&T, CFO, CRO and Capital Modelling team in formulating capital efficient solutions, including reinsurance contracts (both intergroup and external), during the business planning process.
•
To produce analysis and recommendations to the Group Head of I&T and CFO on optimal debt and equity composition of the group capital stack
•
Produce relevant papers seeking approval from Boards, Finance & Investment Committee, Execs, parent company as required to approve of any strategy changes.
•
To help produce the debt strategy, identifying key banks and their capacity to lend.
Other responsibilities
•
To be a key contact for all capital related queries from China Re
•
To be a key contact for Lloyd’s of London on all capital related matters.
•
To work closely within the Investment & Treasury team to understand future investment and cash flow needs and adjust the capital plans accordingly.
•
To be the main contact on capital planning f0r the capital modelling team.
•
Whilst this role is primarily capital focused we envisage helping the Deputy Head of Investments on pulling together investment analysis on occasion.
Our requirements
Relevant experience
•
Proven experience working in financial services.
•
Insurance industry experience (desirable)
Technical skills
•
Knowledge of capital processes and company balance sheets
•
Excellent Excel, PowerPoint, report writing, Bloomberg skills
Education & Experience
•
Part or fully qualified Actuary or Accountant (long standing experience will be accepted)
Personal skills
•
Highly motivated and confident individual with positive work ethic
•
Excellent at managing own workload and working on own initiative.
ABOUT US
Chaucer is a leading insurance group at Lloyd’s, the world’s specialist insurance market. We help protect industries around the world from the risks they face. Our customers include major airlines, energy companies, shipping groups, global manufacturers and property groups.
Our headquarters are in London, and we have international offices in Bermuda, Copenhagen, Dubai and Singapore to be closer to our clients across the world. To learn more about us please visit our website.
Chaucer is committed to diversity, actively values difference and respects people regardless of the protected characteristics which are outlined in the Equality Act 2010 (UK legislation) as a result of the Equal Treatment Directive 2006 (EU legislation).
A diverse workforce and an inclusive workplace are core to our success as a business and integral to our winning strategy and culture. We recruit from the widest available pool of talent, and our hiring, assessment and selection process is fair, free from bias and one which ensures we select the right person for the job, based on merit. We are committed to promoting a culture that actively values difference, and recognises that everyone has the right to be treated with dignity and respect throughout their employment.
We are open to considering flexible working arrangements for all roles and encourage you to outline your needs during the interview process.

About Analog Devices
Analog Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ: ADI) is a global semiconductor leader that bridges the physical and digital worlds to enable breakthroughs at the Intelligent Edge. ADI combines analog, digital, AI, and software technologies into solutions that combat climate change, reliably connect humans and the world, and help drive advancements in automation and robotics, mobility, healthcare, energy and data centers. With revenue of more than $11 billion in FY25, ADI ensures today's innovators stay Ahead of What's Possible. Learn more at www.analog.com and on LinkedIn and X.
Solutions and Tool Specialist – Functional Safety
About the Role
Safety-critical semiconductor products are growing across every market ADI serves. The Functional Safety Office (FSO) is a global team responsible for independent safety confirmation at the highest integrity levels per ISO 26262, and the tooling and infrastructure that supports that work needs to scale with the portfolio.
This role puts you at the center of that challenge. You will build reusable analysis infrastructure — starting with Medini Analyze component libraries — support the development of training content, and work across multiple product families and design types rather than being embedded in a single program. You will gain broad cross-portfolio exposure to how safety-critical semiconductor products are developed.
This role offers a structured path into functional safety — with mentoring from experienced Safety Specialists, progressive project exposure, and the opportunity to build the tooling infrastructure that shapes how safety engineering scales across ADI. You are not expected to arrive as a functional safety expert. You are expected to arrive as an engineer with a solid foundation in semiconductor product development or quality engineering who wants to build tools, tool interfaces, reusable assets and workflows that improve engineering execution.
Why This Team
The FSO operates as ADI's independent safety authority, working across business units and product families rather than within a single design group. The team is global and high-impact — the tooling and methods you help build here will be used across every safety-critical product ADI ships. You will gain exposure to a breadth of product architectures and safety challenges that few individual contributor roles in the industry offer.
Job Responsibilities:
Support, develop and maintain reusable component libraries in Medini Analyze for safety analysis (FMEDA, FTA, dependent failure analysis) across ADI product families, working alongside the FSO's Safety Specialists to ensure technical accuracy and standards compliance.
Work with the FSO team and BU teams to standardize analysis templates and modeling patterns, and translate product-family-specific safety architectures into reusable, parameterized components that improve consistency and reduce setup time for new assessments.
Support the development of role-based training content for common safety activities including FMEDA execution, safety case construction, and safety requirements writing.
Engage with tool vendors such as Synopsys-Ansys (Medini Analyze) on capability evaluation, feature requests, and user community activities.
Develop functional safety domain expertise through structured mentoring and progressive project exposure, contributing to confirmation reviews and safety assessments as competence develops.
Who You Will Work With:
Day-to-day: You will work alongside the FSO's Safety Specialists around the world, who provide technical direction and mentoring on safety analysis and Medini.
Across the FSO: You will collaborate with Functional Safety Managers and Safety Specialists globally to understand where enablement assets have the highest impact.
Engineering teams: You will work with Design Engineers across business units who are the consumers of the tools, templates, and training content you help build.
Tool vendors: You will participate in vendor engagements with Synopsys-Ansys (Medini Analyze) and others on tool capabilities and integration.
Required Qualifications:
• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Systems Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
• 5+ years of experience in semiconductor design engineering, quality engineering, systems engineering, or a related engineering discipline.
• Solid understanding of semiconductor product development processes and lifecycle.
• Experience with structured analytical methods used in product development such as FMEA, design verification, characterization, simulation, or reliability analysis.
• Experience building reusable technical assets such as component libraries, parameterized templates, structured analysis workflows, or design tools.
• Strong technical communication skills with the ability to translate complex methods into clear, usable guidance for engineering teams.
• Self-directed work style suited to a globally distributed team spanning multiple countries and time zones.
• Willingness to travel approximately 10%, primarily to ADI sites in Europe and the US.
Preferred Qualifications:
• Experience with safety analysis methods specifically (FMEA, FMEDA, FTA) including failure mode identification and classification.
• Experience with Synopsys-Ansys Medini Analyze or comparable safety analysis tools (Isograph, ReliaSoft, APIS IQ, Safety Office).
• Familiarity with functional safety standards (ISO 26262, IEC 61508) at a conceptual level. Direct certification is not required.
• Experience developing training content, structured knowledge management systems, or technical curricula.
• Familiarity with automotive quality standards such as IATF 16949 or development process standards such as ASPICE.
Functional safety is one of the fastest-growing disciplines in semiconductor engineering, and this role gives you a structured way in — with mentoring, real project exposure, and the chance to build infrastructure that engineering teams across ADI rely on. If you've been looking for a role with more cross-portfolio visibility and a longer lever than single-program work, we'd like to hear from you.

Job Description:
How to Apply
Russell Reynolds Recruitment is managing this vacancy on behalf of Ofcom. Please note that this role will close at 00:01 on 25th  of October. Please apply to this role through this link:
Please click here to apply
Purpose and scope of the role
This is a newly created role, reflecting the growing importance of Ofcom’s enforcement work, especially as we implement the Online Safety Act. The Group Director, Enforcement will be a member of Ofcom’s Senior Management Team and report directly to the Chief Executive. They will lead the Enforcement Group, a team of around 110 colleagues, which until now has been part of our wider Legal and Enforcement Group. The Group Director will ensure focus and coherence at a time of growing regulatory responsibilities and increasing complexity in Ofcom’s work.
The Enforcement Group identifies and responds to non-compliance affecting consumers and competition in the online safety, telecommunications and postal sectors, as well as competition matters in broadcasting. It routinely monitors complaints, analyses evidence and takes swift action where we see harm, including opening formal investigations, issuing penalties and seeking redress where appropriate. Its work covers enforcement of both Ofcom’s ex ante regulatory rules, and our ex post competition powers and powers under consumer protection legislation, which we hold concurrently with the Competition and Markets Authority. The group also leads Ofcom’s dispute resolution processes in telecoms, postal services and broadcasting. It works closely on cross-cutting issues with the separate content standards enforcement team in Ofcom’s Broadcasting & Media Group and the criminal licence enforcement function in our Spectrum Group.
The Enforcement Group works extremely closely with policy teams across Ofcom, especially those responsible for online safety, infrastructure and connectivity where the Group is exercising enforcement activity on their behalf. Especially close working is needed to ensure that Ofcom makes coherent choices about where to use enforcement tools, and where supervision or other mechanisms would achieve a better and/or faster outcome for consumers.
As Group Director, you will lead and ultimately be accountable for the work of teams investigating high profile, contentious cases. You will be comfortable making decisions, articulating the rationale behind them, and leading engagement with senior external stakeholders.
We are looking for a strong leader with experience in enforcement who can energise, motivate and provide direction for a highly capable and diverse group, leading with clarity and confidence through ambiguity and change, supporting transformation where required and providing stability during periods of sustained pressure or scrutiny.
A collaborative leadership style is essential, as Ofcom works to a highly matrixed structure across multiple locations. This is particularly important as member of the Senior Management Team, where the Group Director, Enforcement will need to forge strong and constructive relationships to ensure their group works closely in partnership with others.
Key responsibilities
• Lead Ofcom’s overall strategy and approach to enforcement, in close collaboration with other Group Directors, and as part of Ofcom’s wider corporate strategy.
• Lead the Enforcement Group (around 110 colleagues), inspiring and motivating the team, working in close collaboration across Ofcom, including with our Board and professional functions. Ensure the agility, pace and effectiveness of the Enforcement Group for the future, ensuring it attracts, retains and develops diverse talent with the broad range of experience and skills required.
• Oversee the work of the Enforcement Group, delegating responsibility and accountability effectively whilst managing risk across overall strategy, the workplan and portfolio of cases and projects, ensuring they are delivered to time, quality and cost.
• Build very strong working relationships between the Enforcement Group and its policy partners in online safety, infrastructure and connectivity, ensuring that the overall strategy is clear for each area. This includes how decisions are made about whether enforcement or other compliance tools are most appropriate in individual cases.
• Maintain existing strong links between the Enforcement Group and Ofcom’s Legal Group led by our General Counsel, and Ofcom’s other groups.
• As a member of Ofcom’s Senior Management Team, play a full role in leading the whole organization alongside the CEO and other members of SMT, including our transformation programme.
• Act as an independent, authoritative voice internally and externally on all of Ofcom’s key strategic areas / themes, challenging internally and acting as an ambassador externally. Be able to discern the key issues, explain, engage and communicate Ofcom’s strategic focus with credibility at the most senior levels of the industry and to a wide range of stakeholders, including government.

Have you ever wanted to see a clinical trial happen in real time?
This is not monitoring from a distance. At Fortrea Clinical Pharmacology Services in Leeds, CRAs are on site, in the flow of the study, when it matters most.
You see dosing days . You walk the clinic floor. You review data as it is generated, not months later. It is a different way to work as a CRA.
It all happens inside a world-class 100-bed, 65,000 ft² Clinical Research Unit, only 7 minutes from the train station, where life‑saving medicines begin their journey.
We are currently hiring a CRA II to support Phase I–Ib studies. This is:
• Full‑time, permanent job.
• Ideally, you live in Yorkshire or within driving distance of our Drapers Yard Clinical Research Unit.
WHY A CAREER IN EARLY CLINICAL DEVELOPMENT AT FORTREA?
Involved in studies even before they are won (i.e., participating at BID meetings), you will:
Be on-site for the moments sponsors travel the world to witness.
This includes first-in-human dosing days, when you review eligibility, observe dosing and safety procedures in real time, and see decisions unfold as the study begins.
You will also follow PK samples into the lab, and work side by side with clinic, pharmacy, and lab teams during the most critical moments of the study.
Rarely work alone.
Studies are often monitored alongside another CRA, and during busy periods you will find several colleagues on site at the same time.
The Leeds Clinical Research Unit gives you the option to work from the office, collaborate face to face, and build real working relationships with CRAs, CTLs, and clinical teams. You will be part of a global team, closely interacting with our other US Clinics/CRAs.
Modern systems. Higher‑value CRA work
Our clinical systems are built for modern monitoring including remote monitoring. Integrated eSource and EDC reduce mechanical SDV and allow CRAs to focus on data integrity, protocol compliance, and study quality.
The result is higher‑value work, closer to science, and with less administrative burden.
WHAT YOU WILL DO
• Monitor Phase I–Ib studies across Fortrea CRU and selected UK sites
• Perform Process Monitoring, Pre-Study, Site Initiation, Routine Monitoring, and Close‑out visits
• Review source data, protocol compliance, and data quality using modern eSource and EDC systems
• Collaborate closely with clinical, lab, and project teams during fast‑paced study timelines
WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR
• CRA II: minimum 2 years independent site management monitoring experience (including Pre-study, Site Initiation, Process Monitoring, Routine Monitoring and Close-Out Visits) according to monitoring plan requirements, SOPs and ICH GCP guidelines
• Have an understanding of SAE reporting, process production, narratives and follow up of SAEs
• A life science degree or nursing qualification.
• You must be independently eligible to work in the UK.
WHAT WE OFFER
• Salary aligned to level plus (£6,000) car allowance
• Flexible working arrangements
• Exposure to early‑phase science that accelerates CRA development
• A collaborative team environment based in a modern Leeds CRU
• Access to innovative clinical trials technology
• Remote working when not monitoring
Join Fortrea and be part of the stage where medicines are proven safe for the first time.

At Roche you can show up as yourself, embraced for the unique qualities you bring. Our culture encourages personal expression, open dialogue, and genuine connections,  where you are valued, accepted and respected for who you are, allowing you to thrive both personally and professionally. This is how we aim to prevent, stop and cure diseases and ensure everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Join Roche, where every voice matters.
The Position
The Opportunity
Roche, one of the leading global pharmaceutical companies, is delighted to announce the opening of its 2027 internship scheme for UK PhD students to join the Biostatistics team within the Product Development Data Sciences and Analytics (PDD) department located in Welwyn Garden City, UK.
Our biostatistics interns will work full-time for 10 weeks (extendable to 12 weeks) at our Roche Welwyn site under the supervision of experienced statisticians and data scientists. Interns will work on theoretical or applied problems with direct relevance to Roche’s ongoing clinical drug development in therapeutic areas such as oncology, immunology, infectious diseases, ophthalmology, or neuroscience.
There will be opportunities to interact with Roche’s global network of over 600 statisticians and data scientists. In addition to engaging in an exciting research topic, interns will have the opportunity to experience first-hand the work of statisticians and data scientists within the pharmaceutical industry and see how they add value to clinical development plans. Interns will learn both new technical and non-technical skills highly relevant to their future careers. At the end of the internship, students will give a department-wide presentation on their research topic.
Who you are
Applicants must currently be registered on a UK PhD programme with a significant methodological focus on statistics or data science, alongside relevant research experience within areas such as biostatistics/epidemiologists, statistics or mathematics, ideally but not necessarily with experience in the health sector. Applicants are required to have successfully passed their initial annual PhD review (typically held at 10-15 months) and must not have completed their PhD viva voce before the application closing date.
Application Process
Applications close on Friday, 13 November 2026. The application process may be extended beyond this date but could close at any point after this time.
Phase I: CV and Cover Letter Review (Your cover letter should not exceed two pages.)
As part of your cover letter, Roche is keen to understand your motivation in applying for this position. Also please include the following information:
• An introduction about yourself, confirming your availability for the face-to-face interview.
• Information about your PhD programme, current PhD status and year, confirmation that you have passed the initial annual review, and the expected viva voce date/year.
• A list of methodological or applied projects you have worked on in your PhD thesis, master’s dissertation, substantial undergraduate projects or previous internships and extracurricular activities, highlighting those within the relevant areas listed in the Requirements section.
• An explanation of why you are interested in the Roche internship programme, highlighting any relevant experience with health & medicine, biology, clinical trials or other non-statistical topics relevant to Roche.
• A description of broad areas (and specific topics, if you have any) in which you would be interested in working during the internship.
• A description of any skills or experience you have relevant to the role, such as team-working, multidisciplinary communication skills, etc.
• An explanation of whether you are eligible to work in the UK, have any visa restrictions or considerations regarding the paid/unpaid pathway, etc.
As an appendix to your cover letter, you can optionally attach a deliverable about one methodological or applied research project you have worked on and (nearly) completed, such as a published paper, working paper, master’s dissertation, or project report.
Phase II: In-person interview: Applicants should be available for a face-to-face interview in Welwyn Garden City on Friday 5th February 2027.
Please note:  Unfortunately visa sponsorship is not available for this role. Candidates must already hold valid authorisation to work in the UK.
Remuneration
Roche offers a competitive salary to a limited number of interns, who would normally be expected to pause their PhD stipend. For applicants from PhD programmes in which internships are an integral part of their PhD training (e.g., via the "Leave to Work Away" route while remaining registered in their PhD programme and continuing to receive the PhD stipend) or for those with visa-related restrictions, Roche can offer an unpaid internship, with alternative support to be agreed on a case-by-case basis. Authorisation from the university will normally be required to confirm the arrangement of the internship.
Working Environment and Culture
Roche offers the excellent benefits you would expect from a blue-chip organisation. There is a fully equipped gym on-site, a library and information centre, and an active sports and social club. We also have a subsidised staff restaurant providing food to cater to every taste throughout the day. At the heart of the building is an informal meeting area known as ‘The Street,’ which features a coffee shop, snack machines and cashpoint. A second building on-site, called ‘The Hub,’ contains modern meeting rooms and conference facilities.
Roche promotes personal well-being and work-life balance; therefore, flexible working options will be considered for all roles at Roche UK. Roche is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive environment. We foster diversity, equity and inclusion to reflect the communities we serve. When addressing healthcare on a global scale, diversity is essential to success. We believe that inclusion is key to understanding people’s varied healthcare needs. Together, we embrace individuality and share a passion for exceptional care. Join Roche, where every voice matters.
Who we are
A healthier future drives us to innovate. Together, more than 100’000 employees across the globe are dedicated to advance science, ensuring everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Our efforts result in more than 26 million people treated with our medicines and over 30 billion tests conducted using our Diagnostics products. We empower each other to explore new possibilities, foster creativity, and keep our ambitions high, so we can deliver life-changing healthcare solutions that make a global impact.
Let’s build a healthier future, together.

About the Role
We are looking for an experienced Compliance Business Partner to provide specialist advice and support across the wider UK financial services compliance framework. This is a hands-on role where you will act as a subject matter expert on current and upcoming regulatory requirements, helping the business identify emerging risks, embed effective controls, and safely deliver new initiatives. You will play a critical part in translating complex regulatory requirements into practical business strategies.
What you’ll do
• Act as the Compliance subject matter expert for the UK business, specifically on our regulatory requirements.
• Provide vital compliance input and risk assessments for new products, customer journeys, partnerships, and strategic business initiatives.
• Maintain a broad understanding of the UK financial services regulatory environment to advise on critical areas such as Consumer Duty, Conduct risk, and Financial crime.

• Significant compliance experience within UK financial services, backed by strong specialist knowledge of electronic money, payment services, and payments regulation.

• Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret ambiguous legislation and translate it into practical business requirements.
• Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the confidence to challenge senior stakeholders and clearly explain complex regulatory concepts to non-specialists.
Where and how you'll work
This is a permanent position based in either our London or Nottingham office.

We invest in the growth of our people alongside our business. You will have extensive opportunities to learn and develop your career, including access to up to £5,000 in funding for external qualifications.

• Wealth & Future: Competitive pension and performance-based bonus schemes
• Holidays: Start with 25 days of annual leave, increasing with tenure. Need more? You have the option to buy 5 additional days.
• Health: Access premium care through our private medical insurance.
• Family Support: We champion your milestones with enhanced parental leave.
A full list of our benefits is available here.

We pride ourselves on hiring the best people, not the same people. Building diverse and inclusive teams is the right thing to do and the smart thing to do. We want to work with top talent: whoever you are, whatever you look like, wherever you come from. We know it’s about what you do, not just what you say. That’s why we make our recruitment process fair and accessible.
We value diversity, inclusion and belonging at our core. We empower our associates to do great work by creating an inclusive culture—one that values diverse perspectives, fosters collaboration and encourages innovative ideas—and a place where associates of all backgrounds can thrive by bringing their most authentic selves to work. We call this our Culture of Belonging, and it rests at the heart of our business.
Our associate-led Business Resource Groups were created to help support our diverse population and include over 10 groups across our offices. Because each Business Resource Group is as unique as the population it serves, they offer a range of activities, networking opportunities, special events and learning programmes to associates.

Your Team:
This role sits within the Product function, in the Trading & Investments domain, reporting into the Head of Product. Savings & Cards is one of five product teams in the domain, and its purpose is to extend client trust beyond investing into everyday saving and spending. You will use AI tools and work closely with engineering, design, compliance, legal, and marketing to define and deliver the savings and cards proposition. You’ll also work closely with the Lifecycle teams, as these products are designed to broaden IG’s customer base and connect saving, spending and investing into one client relationship. The team operates at the intersection of product craft and commercial ambition, focused on building experiences that make saving, spending and investing feel effortless for IG’s customers.
Your role in the Team’s Success:
This is a role for a Senior PM who is as comfortable defining the strategy as they are shipping against it, and who is excited by building something new. As Senior Product Manager for Savings & Cards, you will own the product vision and multi-quarter roadmap for IG’s move into everyday saving and spending, determining which problems are worth solving, setting direction, and driving execution end to end. • Deep curiosity about customer financial behaviour: you understand what makes people start saving or investing, stop, switch, or stay.
• AI-native working style: you already use AI tools (LLMs, prototyping tools, research synthesis, workflow automation) to move faster and think better.
• Comfortable with ambiguity: you can define the problem when the brief doesn’t exist yet.

• Obsession with customer experience: you sweat the details that make journeys feel effortless.
• Regulatory intuition: you can navigate compliance without it becoming a blocker to great UX.
• Evidence and data-driven: you define metrics, run experiments, and make calls based on what works.

Desirable:

As a Navigation Electronic Warfare Engineer, you will support vital work ensuring that MBDA missiles are able to navigate effectively in the most challenging electronic warfare environments.
Salary: £24,460 (pro-rata)
Dynamic working: 5 days per week on-site due to workload classification and need for access to site test facilities
Security clearance: British Citizen or a Dual UK national with British citizenship.
Restrictions and/or limitations relating to nationality and/or rights to work may apply. As a minimum and after offer stage, all successful candidates will need to undergo HMG Basic Personnel Security Standard checks (BPSS), which are managed by the MBDA Personnel Security Team.
This role is scheduled to close for applications at midnight on Monday 4th January 2027 but may close earlier depending on application volumes.
What we can offer you:
•
10 week placement: Starting June 2027, that allows you to apply your university learning to real-world projects and technologies
•
Perform well on your placement and you could secure a graduate role before your final year
•
Pension: Maximum total (employer and employee) contribution of up to 14%
•
Overtime: Opportunity for paid overtime
•
Annual Leave: 5 days
•
Facilities: Fantastic site facilities including subsidised meals, free car parking and much more…
The opportunity:
MBDA Missiles cannot complete their missions without critical Navigation Sensors on board, withstanding enemy interference and providing robust navigation data to guide the missile to the target. Your work will directly influence the design of real missiles, with frequent exposure to high-profile, fast-paced projects.
The Navigation Sensors Group are responsible for the design of the missile navigation subsystems, including identifying and testing equipment from specialist manufacturers – this includes GPS receivers, anti-jam equipment, and Inertial Measurement Units.
You can choose to be based at either our Stevenage or Bristol site. Over the course of your 10-week placement you’ll get involved in:
•
Supporting tests and trials to evaluate and assess navigation equipment performance
•
Hands-on research and design activities to develop the next generation of navigation equipment
•
Monitoring supplier and technology developments and identifying future technologies
•
Collaborating with suppliers and researchers for the development and maturation of new and emerging technology
•
Investigating engineering problems and conducting rapid technical analyses
In this role, you’ll work in a varied and dynamic environment, including as part of an international team with our colleagues in MBDA France and the wider MBDA Group. You’ll work alongside other departments to increase your knowledge on the complexities of a missile, including datalinks, seekers and sensors, and work closely with Integration and System Validation teams.
The work is technically challenging, innovative and rewarding. You’ll be working alongside experienced engineers who will encourage and help you develop the skills required to be an effective Navigation Electronic Warfare
What we're looking for from you:
Current undergraduate working towards a degree in a Physics, Mathematics, Electronics, or Engineering discipline.

Prior experience supporting KYC transformation in a global financial institution;

Knowledge of business(es), products and services.

Strong teamwork and communication skills

This is an FTC role to provide Maternity leave cover for the Property and Treaty Lead role within Chaucer’s Exposure Management Team, across all Property and Treaty business. monitoring aggregate usage, and maintaining a complete and accurate portfolio of accounts.

Essential

• Team management experience

Essential
• Excellent numeracy skills with a good understanding of probability and statistics

Desirable
• Knowledge of GIS and/or other mapping software
• Knowledge of or interest in programming languages, including R and Python

• Excellent organisational skills and able to meet deadlines and objectives

At Roche you can show up as yourself, embraced for the unique qualities you bring. Our culture encourages personal expression, open dialogue, and genuine connections,  where you are valued, accepted and respected for who you are, allowing you to thrive both personally and professionally. This is how we aim to prevent, stop and cure diseases and ensure everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Join Roche, where every voice matters.
The Position
Obesity is one of the UK's greatest and fastest-growing health challenges — a driver of cardiovascular, renal and metabolic disease that touches millions of lives. As a Medical Affairs Partner in our Cardiovascular, Renal & Metabolism (CVRM) team—a dynamic hybrid role that explicitly combines the field-based engagement of a Medical Science Liaison (MSL) with the strategic, internal remit of a Medical Advisor—you will help shape how Roche brings the next generation of obesity and weight-management science to the healthcare professionals and patients who need it. This is a rare opportunity to build our medical presence from the ground up, in the critical pre-launch window where the groundwork you lay determines the difference we make.
Why this role matters: Working one to two years ahead of launch, you will map the UK obesity landscape and build the scientific relationships that ensure the right patients can benefit the moment new options become available. Every conversation with a clinician, every insight you surface, and every piece of evidence you translate helps Roche deliver better outcomes to more patients, faster — and helps healthcare providers prepare to change lives at scale. You won't just support a launch; you will help lay the foundations of how Roche shows up in obesity care in the UK.
The Opportunity:
• Operating seamlessly across both MSL and Medical Advisor capacities, you engage prolifically and meaningfully with healthcare professionals and key opinion leaders across obesity, weight management and the wider cardiometabolic landscape.
• You bring deep therapy-area and scientific expertise, acting as both an external field liaison and an internal strategic advisor to translate complex evidence into meaningful medical value for customers and patients.
• You work with genuine autonomy — creating and adapting high-quality, compliant medical and scientific materials largely independently.
• You map the external scientific landscape and generate insights that shape medical and squad priorities.
• You safeguard the highest standards of compliance, ethics and patient safety, putting patients at the centre of every action.
• You collaborate across teams to remove silos and duplication, and increasingly coach and support colleagues as our team grows.
Who you are:
• You hold a life-sciences, pharmacy or medical qualification and bring strong scientific credibility.
• You have proven experience in medical affairs and are comfortable executing the combined responsibilities of this role (ideally bringing background experience as both a Medical Science Liaison and a Medical Advisor).
• You bring demonstrable experience in obesity / weight management or an adjacent cardiometabolic therapy area.
• You are a confident, self-sufficient operator who structures your own priorities and delivers with minimal support.
• You have a sound working knowledge of the ABPI Code of Practice and act as a guardian of compliance and ethics.
Preferred:
• Experience mentoring or coaching colleagues, or early demonstration of leadership behaviours.
• Experience working in agile, squad-based or self-managed team environments.
If you want your science to make a real difference for people living with obesity and cardiometabolic disease, apply now and help us deliver better outcomes to more patients, faster.
Who we are
A healthier future drives us to innovate. Together, more than 100’000 employees across the globe are dedicated to advance science, ensuring everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Our efforts result in more than 26 million people treated with our medicines and over 30 billion tests conducted using our Diagnostics products. We empower each other to explore new possibilities, foster creativity, and keep our ambitions high, so we can deliver life-changing healthcare solutions that make a global impact.
Let’s build a healthier future, together.

Position Summary
We are seeking an exceptional technology leader to join the Global Portfolio Solutions (GPS) team. This individual will serve as the Chief Technology Officer throughout EMEA partnering with portfolio management teams, deal teams, and GPS functional peers to accelerate technology-driven value creation across Carlyle’s European private equity portfolio.
This role will be the connective tissue between Carlyle’s investment professionals and the technology leadership at our portfolio companies – translating strategic investment theses into concrete technology execution roadmaps, and converting lessons learned across the portfolio into scalable playbooks, partnerships, and community.
Above all, this person will serve as a trusted thought partner to deal teams and portfolio company technology leaders alike – leveraging deep technical and operational expertise, strong listening skills, and a practitioner’s credibility to drive outsized technology value creation across the portfolio. This is not a single-company CTO role: this role operates as a trusted advisor across many companies at once, prioritizing where senior technology leadership drives the most enterprise value.
The ideal hire is a technology executive with current or prior experience as a CTO in the software industry, working across a portfolio of European mid-market B2B technology and SaaS businesses.  Fluency in French and/or German, in addition to English, is strongly preferred.
In-Office Requirement: 4 days a week
Primary Responsibilities
• Define and drive software development / engineering value-creation agendas across technology portfolio companies — product architecture, scalability, technical debt, cloud modernization, AI in SDLC and AI in Product .
• Partner directly with portfolio management teams, deal teams, and GPS functional peers to develop and execute technology value creation roadmaps aligned to each company’s investment thesis and stage of ownership.
Diligence & Assessment
• Support technical diligence on new investments; assess engineering organizations, tech stacks, product roadmap maturity, platform scalability, engineering capabilities and technical debt.
• Translate findings into actionable value-creation plans and contribute technology perspectives to investment committee materials and investment decisions.
• undefined
• Build, curate and manage a network of trusted third-party software engineering  partners — implementation firms, specialist advisors, fractional leaders and vendors — to deliver software engineering execution at portfolio companies
• undefined
• Coach and mentor portfolio-company CTOs and engineering leaders; help assess, recruit and upgrade technology leadership where needed.
• undefined
• Establish reusable playbooks, benchmarks and best practices; drive cross-portfolio knowledge sharing.
• Build connectivity among portfolio CTOs through peer forums and other community-building initiatives
• undefined
• Position technology assets for exit by articulating the equity story, de-risking the stack, and evidencing scalability to buyers.
Qualifications
The candidate will be a highly-accomplished technology executive or senior practitioner having served as a CTO, or equivalent, ideally at a PE- or venture-backed company that has successfully executed a meaningful technology transformation. In addition, they will have:
• Deep, current expertise across product engineering and software architecture,  AI within the software development lifecycle.
• Demonstrated experience leading or overseeing meaningful software transformations, ideally within mid-market B2B software or SaaS businesses, and translating technology investment into measurable outcomes such as revenue growth, cost reduction, margin expansion or increased enterprise value.
• Track record designing and optimizing technology operating models, including organizational structures, onshore/offshore models, platform teams, vendor strategies and other approaches to improving engineering effectiveness and efficiency.
• Familiarity with the private equity investment lifecycle, including technology diligence, value-creation planning, portfolio-company execution and exit readiness. Direct experience in a PE portfolio or operating-partner environment is preferred.
• Experience building and leveraging networks of technology partners, specialist advisors and vendors to accelerate execution while maintaining a lean operating model.
• Demonstrated ability to operate effectively across multiple businesses, priorities, geographies and cultures, within a European context.
Competencies & Attributes
• Investor mindset. Able to identify the technology issues that materially affect business performance and translate them into P&L, valuation and investment outcomes.
• Commercial and pragmatic. Focuses on the interventions that create the greatest value rather than pursuing technology for its own sake; able to articulate impact clearly and concisely to financial and investment professionals.
• Influence without authority. Credible with founders, CEOs, CTOs/CIOs, management teams, boards and investment professionals; able to challenge constructively and drive action through others.
• Adaptable advisor. Able to diagnose the needs of different portfolio companies and improve performance through consultation and collaboration rather than applying a one-size-fits-all approach.
• Bias to action. Comfortable with ambiguity and competing priorities; exercises sound judgment about where to engage deeply and where to operate through management teams, partners and advisors.
• Collaborative and low ego. Works effectively within a team of functional experts, shares knowledge and best practices, and invests in developing portfolio-company technology leaders.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the executive presence and judgment to operate effectively with senior management teams and investment professionals.
• Fluency in German and/or French required.
​
Who We Are
When people, ideas, and capital come together, opportunity expands across private markets. At Carlyle, this belief has shaped how we invest for decades, fueling growth for companies and delivering performance for investors.
Visit our website to learn more about our firm and the ways our platform is shaping private markets.

The Principal Analog Design Engineer is responsible for leading the design and development of high-speed analog ICs from concept through to volume production.
This role serves as a key technical authority within the team, driving innovation in circuit architecture, leading chip development projects, and ensuring high-performance, manufacturable designs that meet product and customer requirements.

• Proven experience as a technical lead on chip development projects.
• Strong RF analog design experience (10 GHz+).
• Expert proficiency with Cadence design and simulation tools.
• Solid understanding of RF/analog layout techniques, including parasitics, matching, ESD, crosstalk, and IR drop.
